definition_zh: n. 旋转木马；（机场）行李传送带
definition_en: a fairground ride with model horses that turn in a circle; a moving belt that brings luggage to passengers
core_image: 彩绘木马绕着灯柱一圈圈起伏
scene: 孩子们爬上彩绘木马，音乐响起，整座旋转木马慢慢转起来。The children climbed onto the painted horses as the carousel began to turn.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：carousel 指旋转木马；句意是孩子们骑上彩绘木马，它随着音乐转动。

senses.title: The fairground ride
senses.definition: a ride at a fair with model horses that go round to music
senses.definitionCN: 游乐场里随音乐转圈的骑马设施
senses.example: She waved from a white carousel horse.
senses.exampleCN: 她骑在一匹白色的木马上挥手。
senses.why: The name came from French carrousel, a display of horsemanship.
senses.whyCN: 名称来自法语 carrousel，指马术表演。

senses.title: The luggage belt
senses.definition: a moving belt that brings suitcases to passengers at an airport
senses.definitionCN: 机场里把行李箱送到旅客面前的循环传送带
senses.example: Our bags were already on the carousel.
senses.exampleCN: 我们的箱子已经在传送带上了。
senses.why: Airports borrowed the turning image for the luggage loop.
senses.whyCN: 机场借用了转圈的形象来指行李环带。

intro.en: Carousel comes from French carrousel, a showy display of horsemanship at court.
intro.cn: carousel 源自法语 carrousel，指宫廷里华丽的马术表演。

items.en: Italian carosello names a tournament of horsemen.
items.cn: 十六世纪意大利语 carosello 指骑手竞技。

items.en: French carrousel names a court riding display.
items.cn: 十七世纪法语 carrousel 指宫廷马术表演。

items.en: Travelling fairs build wooden horses on a wheel.
items.cn: 十八世纪流动集市造出装在轮上的木马。

items.en: Steam power turns the ride faster and smoother.
items.cn: 十九世纪蒸汽让旋转更稳更快。

items.en: The same turning idea names the luggage belt.
items.cn: 二十世纪同样的转圈意象用来指行李带。

note.en: The look-alike group turns on the car- opening; the near-meaning group gathers fairground rides and moving belts.
note.cn: 形近组围绕 car- 开头；近义组收拢游乐设施与循环传送带。

entries.definition: To hold and move something.
A joyful song, often at Christmas.
A unit for gems or gold.
A round ride with animals.
A moving band that carries items.
A wooden horse on the ride.

normalIntro.en: A carousel is a circle of horses that keeps coming back to where it began.
normalIntro.cn: carousel 是一圈不断回到原点的木马。

normal.en: Carrousel was a court riding show.
normal.cn: carrousel 是宫廷马术表演。

normal.en: Fairs put wooden horses on a wheel.
normal.cn: 集市把木马装到轮子上。

normal.en: Music and lights go round with them.
normal.cn: 音乐和灯随着它们转。

normal.en: At airports the belt also goes round.
normal.cn: 机场的传送带也在转圈。

normal.en: One word covers both circles.
normal.cn: 一个词覆盖两种转圈。

abstract.en: A ring of painted animals that never arrives.
abstract.cn: 一圈彩绘动物，永远到不了终点。

abstract.en: A circle that sells the feeling of travel.
abstract.cn: 一个兜售旅行感的圆圈。

abstract.en: Luggage taking the long way to your hands.
abstract.cn: 行李绕远路来到你手上。

examples.en: The carousel stopped and the children ran to the next ride.
examples.cn: 旋转木马停下，孩子们跑向下一个项目。

examples.en: Our flight was delayed, so we waited by the baggage carousel.
examples.cn: 航班延误，我们在行李转盘旁等。

examples.en: The fair had two carousels side by side.
examples.cn: 集市上并排有两座旋转木马。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「卡喽赛尔」——木马转到卡住，大家还在塞着排队。

root: 法语 carrousel（马术表演）→ 英语 carousel

sensesIntro.en: The ride and the airport belt share one shape: a loop that brings things back to the same point.
sensesIntro.cn: 游乐设施与机场传送带共享一个形状：把东西送回同一点的环。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: painted horses rising and falling around a lighted pole
core.cn: 核心意象：彩绘木马绕着灯柱起伏转圈

branches.en: A child waving from a white horse.
branches.cn: 孩子骑在白马上挥手。

branches.en: Music and bulbs on a summer evening.
branches.cn: 夏夜里的音乐与灯泡。

branches.en: Suitcases sliding into view.
branches.cn: 行李箱滑到眼前。

branches.en: A crowd watching one belt.
branches.cn: 一群人盯着同一条传送带。

branches.en: A loop that always returns.
branches.cn: 总回到原点的环。

intro.en: The word is a French loan; the list below adds the vocabulary of rides, circles and travel.
intro.cn: 这个词是法语借词；下面列出游乐、圆圈、旅行词场的词缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin circus is a ring, rota is a wheel, and vehere is to carry.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 circus 意为圆环，rota 意为轮子，vehere 意为运送。

latinEntries.exampleCN: circus 产生 circle 与 circuit。
rota 产生 rotate 与 rotary。
vehere 产生 vehicle 与 vector。

definition_zh: n. 拼车，合用汽车；拼车的一群人；v. 拼车出行
definition_en: a group of people who share one car for regular journeys; to travel together in one car
core_image: 几位同事挤进同一辆车去上班
scene: 为了省油，几位同事约定拼车上班，轮流开车。To save fuel, the colleagues carpool to work and take turns driving.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：carpool 指拼车；句意是同事为省油轮流开车一起上班。

senses.title: The shared ride
senses.definition: an arrangement in which several people travel together in one car
senses.definitionCN: 几个人同乘一辆车的安排
senses.example: Our carpool leaves at seven sharp.
senses.exampleCN: 我们的拼车七点整出发。
senses.why: The word joins car and pool, a shared supply.
senses.whyCN: 该词由 car 与 pool（共用资源）合成。

senses.title: To share a car
senses.definition: to travel in one car with others on a regular route
senses.definitionCN: 按固定路线与他人同车出行
senses.example: She carpools with two neighbours.
senses.exampleCN: 她和两位邻居拼车。
senses.why: The noun became a verb by simple conversion.
senses.whyCN: 名词直接转为动词。

intro.en: Carpool joins car with pool, a shared fund of people or things, a pattern from the nineteen forties.
intro.cn: carpool 由 car 与 pool（共用的人员或资源）组合，这种构词见于二十世纪四十年代。

items.en: Car shortens carriage and spreads worldwide.
items.cn: 二十世纪初 car 由 carriage 缩短并通行。

items.en: Pool means a shared fund or supply.
items.cn: 十七世纪 pool 指共用的资金或资源。

items.en: Wartime fuel rules push shared rides.
items.cn: 四十年代战时燃油限制推动合乘。

items.en: Cities open carpool lanes for shared cars.
items.cn: 七十年代城市为合乘车设专用道。

items.en: Apps match strangers for daily carpools.
items.cn: 本世纪应用为陌生人匹配日常拼车。

note.en: The look-alike group echoes the car- opening; the near-meaning group covers shared travel and public transport.
note.cn: 形近组呼应 car- 开头；近义组涵盖合乘与公共交通。

entries.definition: A roofed shelter for a car.
A humorous drawing or film.
A freshwater fish.
A service matching drivers and riders.
A shared van for commuters.
To travel to and from work.

normalIntro.en: A carpool is a car treated like a shared well: everyone draws from the same one.
normalIntro.cn: carpool 是把车当成共用井：大家从同一口井取水。

normal.en: Car means the vehicle.
normal.cn: car 指车辆。

normal.en: Pool means a shared supply.
normal.cn: pool 指共用的资源。

normal.en: Put them together and the car is shared.
normal.cn: 合起来就是共用一辆车。

normal.en: Drivers take turns at the wheel.
normal.cn: 司机轮流掌方向盘。

normal.en: The word also works as a verb.
normal.cn: 这个词也能作动词。

abstract.en: A private seat made slightly public.
abstract.cn: 被稍微公开的私人座位。

abstract.en: Four people agreeing on one route.
abstract.cn: 四个人就一条路线达成一致。

abstract.en: Traffic thinned by a small promise.
abstract.cn: 靠一个小约定变稀的车流。

examples.en: The carpool meets outside the library every morning.
examples.cn: 拼车每天早上在图书馆外集合。

examples.en: He started to carpool after petrol prices rose.
examples.cn: 油价上涨后他开始拼车。

examples.en: Two carpools share the same parking space.
examples.cn: 两支拼车队共用同一个停车位。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「卡普」——车子卡在路上的时候，普普通通的拼车最有用了。

root: 英语 car（车）+ pool（共用资源）→ carpool

sensesIntro.en: A shared car and the act of sharing it are one idea seen from two sides.
sensesIntro.cn: 合用的车与合用这件事，是同一想法的两面。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: colleagues squeezing into one car before dawn
core.cn: 核心意象：天亮前同事们挤进同一辆车

branches.en: A seat offered to a neighbour.
branches.cn: 把一个座位让给邻居。

branches.en: A line of cars with three people each.
branches.cn: 每辆坐三人的车队。

branches.en: Keys passed around the group.
branches.cn: 钥匙在小组里轮转。

branches.en: A quieter road at eight in the morning.
branches.cn: 早晨八点安静些的路。

branches.en: A car that behaves like a bus.
branches.cn: 行为像公交的私家车。

intro.en: Carpool is an English compound; the list below adds words for vehicles, sharing and travel.
intro.cn: carpool 是英语复合词；下面列出车辆、共用、出行词场的词缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin carrus is a wagon, and socius is a partner.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 carrus 意为马车，socius 意为伙伴。

latinEntries.exampleCN: carrus 产生 car 与 carriage。
socius 产生 social 与 society。
via 产生 deviate 与 obvious。

definition_zh: 马车；车厢；运输
definition_en: a vehicle with wheels pulled by horses, or a separate section of a train
core_image: 一个带轮的车厢，被马或机车拉着往前走
scene: 马车沿着乡间小路慢慢走。The carriage moved slowly along the country road.
sceneCN: 这里 carriage 是「马车」（第 1 个义项：由马拉的四轮载客车）；句意是马车沿着乡间小路慢慢走。

derivatives.zh: 与 carriage 同根，义为「携带、运送」
carry 加 -er 构成，义为「承运人、携带者」
carriage 与 way 复合，义为「车行道」

senses.title: A horse-drawn passenger vehicle
senses.definition: a wheeled vehicle pulled by horses and used for carrying passengers
senses.definitionCN: 由马拉动、用来载客的四轮车辆
senses.example: They hired a carriage for the wedding.
senses.exampleCN: 他们为婚礼租了一辆马车。
senses.why: Old French cariage meant the act of carrying, and the vehicle that carried people took the name.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 cariage 意为「运送」，用来载人的车便承接了这个名字。

senses.title: A separate section of a train
senses.definition: one of the separate parts of a train where passengers sit
senses.definitionCN: 列车中供乘客乘坐的一节独立部分
senses.example: We found seats in the last carriage.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在最后一节车厢找到了座位。
senses.why: A railway carriage is the same wheeled passenger box, now pulled by an engine.
senses.whyCN: 火车车厢就是同一个载人带轮盒子，只是改由机车牵引。

senses.title: The transport of goods
senses.definition: the business or cost of moving goods from one place to another
senses.definitionCN: 把货物从一处运到另一处的业务或费用
senses.example: The contract covers the carriage of goods by sea.
senses.exampleCN: 这份合同涵盖海运货物运输。
senses.why: The oldest abstract sense is simply carrying, which survives in trade and legal language.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的抽象义就是「运送」，它保留在贸易与法律用语中。

intro.en: Carriage first meant the act of carrying, then the vehicle that does the carrying.
intro.cn: carriage 最初指「运送」这个动作，后来指执行运送的车辆。

items.en: carrus named a wagon, the root of the whole carrying family.
items.cn: carrus 指马车，是整组「运送」词汇的根。

items.en: carricare meant to load a cart with goods.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 carricare 意为「往车上装货」。

items.en: cariage named the act of transporting and the charge for it.
items.cn: 古法语 cariage 指运输行为及其费用。

items.en: English borrowed carriage for transport, then for the coach that carried people.
items.cn: 英语借入 carriage 指运输，随后指载人的马车。

items.en: Railways gave the word its sense of a passenger car, which remains in British English.
items.cn: 铁路赋予它「客车车厢」的义项，这一用法保留在英式英语中。

note.en: Carriage is the vehicle and the act, and it shares its root with carry and cargo.
note.cn: carriage 既是车辆也是行为，并与 carry、cargo 同根。

entries.definition: to hold something and take it somewhere
entries.definitionCN: 携带、运送，与 carriage 同根。

entries.definition: a person or company that transports goods
entries.definitionCN: 承运人、运输公司，由 carry 加 -er 构成。

entries.definition: goods carried by ship or aircraft
entries.definitionCN: 船或飞机运载的货物，与 carriage 同出 carricare。

entries.definition: a strong four-wheeled vehicle for loads
entries.definitionCN: 结实的四轮载货车，与马车同类。

entries.definition: a comfortable bus or a horse-drawn passenger vehicle
entries.definitionCN: 舒适的长途客车，或旧时的载客马车。

entries.definition: a small vehicle pushed or pulled by hand or animal

normalIntro.en: Carriage is the noun of carrying: the act first, the vehicle second.
normalIntro.cn: carriage 是「运送」的名词：先有动作，后有车辆。

normal.en: carriage and carry share the same root, from Latin carricare, to load.
normal.cn: carriage 与 carry 同根，来自拉丁语 carricare（装车）。

normal.en: The -age ending often makes a noun of action, as in carriage and marriage.
normal.cn: -age 结尾常把动作变成名词，如 carriage、marriage。

normal.en: railway carriage is the British term for a passenger car.
normal.cn: railway carriage 是英式英语里「客车车厢」的说法。

normal.en: carriage of goods keeps the abstract transport sense in legal writing.
normal.cn: carriage of goods 在法律文本里保留了抽象的「货运」义。

normal.en: baby carriage is the American term for a pram.
normal.cn: baby carriage 是美式英语中的「婴儿推车」。

abstract.en: Picture four wheels, a wooden box, and two horses pulling it along a lane.
abstract.cn: 想象四个轮子、一个木箱，两匹马拉着它沿小路走。

abstract.en: Picture a train made of separate boxes linked one behind another.
abstract.cn: 想象一列火车由一节节独立盒子前后相连。

abstract.en: Picture boxes being weighed and marked before a long journey.
abstract.cn: 想象箱子在长途运输前被称重、做标记。

examples.en: The carriage moved slowly along the country road.
examples.cn: 马车沿着乡间小路慢慢走。

examples.en: We found seats in the last carriage.
examples.cn: 我们在最后一节车厢找到了座位。

examples.en: The contract covers the carriage of goods by sea.
examples.cn: 这份合同涵盖海运货物运输。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「开瑞吉」——车拉着人一路往前，轮子吱吱作响。

root: 拉丁语 carrus（车）→ 晚期拉丁语 carricare（装车）→ 古法语 cariage（运送）→ 英语 carriage。

sensesIntro.en: The act of carrying becomes the vehicle that carries, on road and on rail.
sensesIntro.cn: 「运送」这个动作变成了执行运送的车辆，公路上与铁路上都是。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wheeled box being pulled along with people or goods inside.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个带轮盒子被人或货装满，正被拉着走。

branches.en: The road sense: a horse-drawn vehicle for passengers.
branches.cn: 公路义：由马拉的载客车辆。

branches.en: The rail sense: one passenger section of a train.
branches.cn: 铁路义：列车的一节载客车厢。

branches.en: The trade sense: the business and cost of moving goods.
branches.cn: 贸易义：运送货物的业务与费用。

branches.en: Both vehicle senses keep the same box on wheels, only the power changes.
branches.cn: 两个车辆义都是同一个带轮盒子，只是动力来源不同。

branches.en: carriage of goods survives mainly in contracts and shipping documents.
branches.cn: carriage of goods 主要保留在合同与货运单据中。

intro.en: Carriage is formed on the carrying root with the noun ending -age.
intro.cn: carriage 建立在「运送」词根上，加名词词尾 -age。

latinIntro.en: Latin carrus and carricare are the source of carriage, carry, cargo, and carrier.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 carrus 与 carricare 是 carriage、carry、cargo、carrier 的共同来源。

items.meaning: a passenger vehicle or the act of transporting
items.example: The carriage stopped at the gate.

items.meaning: to take something from one place to another
a person or company that transports goods
goods carried by ship or aircraft
items.example: The cargo was checked at the port.

items.meaning: the part of a road used by vehicles
items.example: The carriageway was closed for repairs.
Carrus stands at the head of the family.
items.exampleCN: carrus 位于这个词族的最前端。

definition_zh: 胡萝卜；诱饵
definition_en: a long orange root vegetable, or something offered as a reward to persuade someone
core_image: 一根橙色的根从土里被拔出来，还带着泥
scene: 她从地里拔出一根胡萝卜。She pulled a carrot out of the ground.
sceneCN: 这里 carrot 是「胡萝卜」（第 1 个义项：一种橙色根菜）；句意是她从地里拔出一根胡萝卜。

collocations.zh: 胡萝卜加大棒；软硬兼施

derivatives.zh: 由 carrot 的词干构成，义为「胡萝卜素」
carrot 加 -y 构成，义为「胡萝卜色的」
carrot 与 top 复合，口语指「红头发的人」

senses.title: The long orange root vegetable
senses.definition: a long pointed orange root eaten as a vegetable
senses.definitionCN: 一种长而尖的橙色根，作为蔬菜食用
senses.example: She cut the carrot into thin slices.
senses.exampleCN: 她把胡萝卜切成薄片。
senses.why: The word came from a Greek name for this root, through Latin and French.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自希腊语对这种根菜的称呼，经拉丁语和法语传来。

senses.title: A reward used to persuade
senses.definition: something attractive offered to persuade someone to act
senses.definitionCN: 用来吸引并说服某人行动的好处
senses.example: The bonus was a carrot to attract new staff.
senses.exampleCN: 奖金是吸引新员工的诱饵。
senses.why: A carrot is held in front of a donkey to make it move, and the image became a metaphor for incentives.
senses.whyCN: 人们把胡萝卜吊在驴子前面让它往前走，这个画面就成了「激励手段」的比喻。

intro.en: Carrot travelled from Greek to Latin to French before reaching English in the sixteenth century.
intro.cn: carrot 从希腊语经拉丁语、法语，在十六世纪进入英语。

items.en: karoton named the carrot plant, a word of uncertain earlier origin.
items.cn: karoton 指胡萝卜这种植物，更早的来源尚不确定。

items.en: carota was the Latin name for the same root vegetable.
items.cn: carota 是拉丁语对同一种根菜的称呼。

items.en: carotte kept the vegetable sense in medieval and early modern French.
items.cn: carotte 在中古及近代早期法语中保留了这一蔬菜义。

items.en: English borrowed the word as carrot, describing the orange root we know.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入为 carrot，指我们今天熟悉的橙色根菜。

items.en: The metaphor of the dangling carrot added the sense of a reward or incentive.
items.cn: 「吊着的胡萝卜」这一比喻又添上了「奖励、激励」的义项。

note.en: Carrot has a chemical relative in carotene, and it sits beside other root vegetables.
note.cn: carrot 在化学词汇里有 carotene 这个亲戚，同时和别的根菜相邻。

entries.definition: the orange substance in carrots that the body turns into vitamin A
entries.definitionCN: 胡萝卜素，胡萝卜中使人体合成维生素甲的橙色物质。

entries.definition: orange-red in colour, like a carrot
entries.definitionCN: 胡萝卜色的，指橙红色，由 carrot 加 -y 构成。

entries.definition: the Latin name for the carrot
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁语中的「胡萝卜」，是英语 carrot 的直接源头。

entries.definition: a round white root vegetable
entries.definitionCN: 圆形的白色根菜，与胡萝卜同属根菜。

entries.definition: a small red or white root with a sharp taste
entries.definitionCN: 小红萝卜或白萝卜，味道辛辣。

entries.definition: a plant grown for food
entries.definitionCN: 作为食物种植的植物，是 carrot 的上位词。

normalIntro.en: One orange root, and a metaphor about donkeys and rewards.
normalIntro.cn: 一根橙色根菜，外加一个关于驴子与奖励的比喻。

normal.en: carrot comes through French carotte from Latin carota.
normal.cn: carrot 经法语 carotte 来自拉丁语 carota。

normal.en: carotene, the orange substance, keeps the same stem.
normal.cn: 橙色的胡萝卜素 carotene 保留了同一个词干。

normal.en: carrot and stick names the two tools of persuasion, reward and threat.
normal.cn: carrot and stick 指奖励与威胁两种手段。

normal.en: grated carrot and carrot cake are common kitchen phrases.
normal.cn: 胡萝卜丝与胡萝卜蛋糕是常见说法。

normal.en: The plural carrots adds only an s.
normal.cn: 复数 carrots 只加一个 s。

abstract.en: Picture a bright orange root pulled from dark soil, soil still clinging to it.
abstract.cn: 想象一根亮橙色的根从黑土里拔出，还带着泥。

abstract.en: Picture a carrot tied to a stick, hanging just ahead of a walking donkey.
abstract.cn: 想象一根胡萝卜系在棍上，吊在行走的驴子前面。

abstract.en: Picture a plate of orange slices next to a green salad.
abstract.cn: 想象一盘橙色薄片旁边放着一份绿色沙拉。

examples.en: She pulled a carrot out of the ground.
examples.cn: 她从地里拔出一根胡萝卜。

examples.en: She cut the carrot into thin slices.
examples.cn: 她把胡萝卜切成薄片。

examples.en: The bonus was a carrot to attract new staff.
examples.cn: 奖金是吸引新员工的诱饵。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「开罗特」——开罗的市场里，特多这种橙色的根菜。

root: 希腊语 karoton → 拉丁语 carota → 法语 carotte → 英语 carrot；同族词有 carotene。

sensesIntro.en: The vegetable comes first; the reward metaphor hangs it in front of someone.
sensesIntro.cn: 先有这种蔬菜，后来「奖励」的比喻把它吊在了人面前。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a long orange root lifted out of the earth.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根长长的橙色根从土里被拔起。

branches.en: The food sense: the orange root eaten raw or cooked.
branches.cn: 食物义：可生吃或熟食的橙色根菜。

branches.en: The incentive sense: a reward dangled to produce action.
branches.cn: 激励义：吊在前面促使人行动的好处。

branches.en: carrot juice and carrot cake show the vegetable in compounds.
branches.cn: 胡萝卜汁与胡萝卜蛋糕展示了这种蔬菜的复合用法。

branches.en: The metaphor works because the vegetable is bright, cheap, and easy to dangle.
branches.cn: 这个比喻成立，是因为胡萝卜颜色醒目、便宜、又容易吊起来。

branches.en: carrot and stick pairs the reward with a threat.
branches.cn: carrot and stick 把奖励与威胁配成一对。

intro.en: Carrot is a base noun of Greek origin; -y and compounds build its family.
intro.cn: carrot 是源自希腊语的基础名词，词族靠 -y 与复合构词扩展。

latinIntro.en: Latin carota is the bridge between Greek karoton and English carrot.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 carota 是希腊语 karoton 与英语 carrot 之间的桥。

items.example: The soup contains carrot and onion.
items.exampleCN: 这汤里有胡萝卜和洋葱。

items.example: The field was full of carrots.

items.meaning: the orange pigment found in carrots

items.exampleCN: 胡萝卜素赋予这种蔬菜颜色。

items.meaningCN: 口语中对红头发者的称呼

items.exampleCN: 上学时大家叫他红头发。

items.example: Carota passed into French as carotte.
items.exampleCN: carota 进入法语后成为 carotte。

items.example: Karoton is the earliest known form.
items.exampleCN: karoton 是目前已知最早的形式。

items.example: The stew had turnip and beef.
items.exampleCN: 这锅炖菜有芜菁和牛肉。

definition_zh: 携带；搬运；运送；支撑
definition_en: to hold something and take it from one place to another
core_image: 双手把东西抱起来，一路带到别处
scene: 他两手抱着箱子走上楼。He carried the box upstairs in both arms.
sceneCN: 这里 carried 是 carry 的过去式，意为「搬运、抱着」（第 1 个义项：用手拿着东西移动）；句意是他两手抱着箱子走上楼。

derivatives.zh: carry 加 -er 构成，义为「承运人、携带者」
与 carry 同根，义为「马车；车厢；运输」
同根名词，义为「船货、货物」

senses.title: To hold and move something
senses.definition: to hold something in your hands or arms while you move
senses.definitionCN: 移动时用手或手臂拿着某物
senses.example: She carried the baby up the stairs.
senses.exampleCN: 她抱着婴儿上楼。
senses.why: The word came from a verb meaning to transport, and the simplest form is carrying by hand.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自表示「运送」的动词，最基本的形式就是用手搬运。

senses.title: To transport goods or passengers
senses.definition: to take goods or people from one place to another in a vehicle
senses.definitionCN: 用交通工具把货物或人从一处运到另一处
senses.example: The train carries hundreds of passengers each day.
senses.exampleCN: 这列火车每天运送数百名乘客。
senses.why: The same verb widens from a person's hands to a ship, train, or plane.
senses.whyCN: 同一个动词从人的双手扩展到船、火车和飞机。

senses.title: To support the weight of something
senses.definition: to support the weight or burden of something
senses.definitionCN: 支撑某物的重量或负担
senses.example: These pillars carry the weight of the roof.
senses.exampleCN: 这些柱子承受屋顶的重量。
senses.why: If you carry a load, you bear its weight, and pillars and beams do the same.
senses.whyCN: 人搬东西时要承受重量，柱子和横梁做的是同一件事。

intro.en: Carry entered English from northern French, and its root goes back to the Latin wagon.
intro.cn: carry 从法国北方方言进入英语，词根可追溯到拉丁语的「车」。

items.en: carrus named a wagon, the distant source of the carrying family.
items.cn: carrus 指马车，是这组「运送」词汇的远源。

items.en: carricare meant to load a cart with goods.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 carricare 意为「往车上装货」。

items.en: carier meant to transport or convey, and it was this form that crossed the Channel.
items.cn: 古北法语 carier 意为「运送、传送」，正是这个形式渡过了海峡。

items.en: carien became the everyday English verb for carrying.
items.cn: carien 成为英语中日常表示「携带」的动词。

items.en: The verb widened to vehicles, loads, responsibilities, and fixed phrases such as carry out.
items.cn: 这个动词扩展到交通工具、负载、责任，以及 carry out 等固定搭配。

note.en: Carry is the base of carrier, carriage, and cargo, and its near meanings split holding from transporting.
note.cn: carry 是 carrier、carriage、cargo 的基础，近义词则把「拿着」与「运输」区分开。

entries.definition: a person or company that transports goods
entries.definitionCN: 承运人、运输公司，由 carry 加 -er 构成。

entries.definition: a horse-drawn vehicle or a railway car
entries.definitionCN: 马车或火车车厢，与 carry 同根。

entries.definition: goods carried by ship or aircraft
entries.definitionCN: 船货、货物，与 carry 同出 carricare。

entries.definition: to carry or support a weight
entries.definitionCN: 承载或支撑重量，比 carry 更书面。

entries.definition: to move goods or people in vehicles
entries.definitionCN: 用交通工具运送货物或人，对应第二个义项。

entries.definition: to keep something in your hands
entries.definitionCN: 把东西拿在手里，是 carry 动作的起点。

normalIntro.en: A short verb whose family shows every stage: hand, vehicle, pillar, phrase.
normalIntro.cn: 一个短动词，词族展示了它的每一站：手、车、柱子、短语。

normal.en: carry, carrier, carriage, and cargo all share one root, from Latin carricare.
normal.cn: carry、carrier、carriage、cargo 共享一个词根，来自拉丁语 carricare。

normal.en: carry on means continue, as if carrying the work forward.
normal.cn: carry on 意为「继续」，像把工作继续搬着往前走。

normal.en: carry out means perform, taking a plan from paper into action.
normal.cn: carry out 意为「执行」，把计划从纸上搬进行动。

normal.en: Pillars carry a roof, which links the verb to support.
normal.cn: 柱子 carry 屋顶，这就把动词和「支撑」连了起来。

normal.en: The third person carries changes y to ies.
normal.cn: 第三人称 carries 把 y 变成 ies。

abstract.en: Picture both arms wrapped around a heavy box, steps slow and even.
abstract.cn: 想象双臂环抱一个重箱子，脚步缓慢而平稳。

abstract.en: Picture a ship moving across water with the weight of goods inside it.
abstract.cn: 想象一艘船载着货物的重量在水面上行进。

abstract.en: Picture a stone pillar holding up a roof without any visible effort.
abstract.cn: 想象一根石柱不动声色地撑起屋顶。

examples.en: He carried the box upstairs in both arms.
examples.cn: 他两手抱着箱子走上楼。

examples.en: The train carries hundreds of passengers each day.
examples.cn: 这列火车每天运送数百名乘客。

examples.en: These pillars carry the weight of the roof.
examples.cn: 这些柱子承受屋顶的重量。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「开瑞」——双手一开一合，把东西一路抱走。

root: 古北法语 carier（运送）→ 中古英语 carien；源头为晚期拉丁语 carricare（装车）与 carrus（车）。

sensesIntro.en: Hands, vehicles, and pillars all carry: they hold something and bear its weight elsewhere.
sensesIntro.cn: 手、车、柱子都在 carry：拿着某物，并把它的重量承住。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: arms wrapped around a load, moving it steadily.
core.cn: 核心意象：双臂环抱着负载，稳稳地移动。

branches.en: The hand sense: holding something while walking.
branches.cn: 手工义：边走边拿着东西。

branches.en: The vehicle sense: a train or ship moving goods and people.
branches.cn: 交通义：火车或船运送货物与人。

branches.en: The structural sense: a pillar bearing weight.
branches.cn: 结构义：柱子承受重量。

branches.en: All senses share holding plus bearing, whether by hand, engine, or stone.
branches.cn: 三个义项都包含「拿着并承重」，只是靠手、发动机还是石头。

branches.en: Phrases such as carry out and carry on extend the verb into abstract action.
branches.cn: carry out 与 carry on 等短语把这个动词延伸到抽象行动。

intro.en: Carry is a base verb; -er and -age build its main noun family.
intro.cn: carry 是基础动词，-er 与 -age 构成它的主要名词词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin carrus and carricare supply the root for carry, carrier, carriage, and cargo.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 carrus 与 carricare 为 carry、carrier、carriage、cargo 提供词根。

the act of holding and moving something

definition_zh: v. 雕刻，刻出；把（熟肉）切成片
definition_en: to cut a shape or pattern into wood, stone or other material; to cut cooked meat into slices
core_image: 刀刃在木头上一点点刻出鸟的形状
scene: 他用一把小刀在木块上雕刻出一只鸟的形状。He used a small knife to carve a bird out of the wood.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：carve 指雕刻；句意是用小刀从木头里刻出一只鸟。

senses.title: Cutting a shape
senses.definition: to cut material to make a shape or design
senses.definitionCN: 切削材料以形成形状或图案
senses.example: The handle was carved from dark wood.
senses.exampleCN: 刀柄用深色木头雕成。
senses.why: Old English ceorfan meant to cut.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 ceorfan 意为切割。

senses.title: Slicing meat
senses.definition: to cut cooked meat into pieces at the table
senses.definitionCN: 在餐桌上把熟肉切成片
senses.example: He carved the roast for the guests.
senses.exampleCN: 他为客人切烤肉。
senses.why: The table sense grew from the same cutting action.
senses.whyCN: 餐桌义项由同一切割动作延伸而来。

intro.en: Carve goes back to Old English ceorfan, to cut, a word shared with Dutch kerven.
intro.cn: carve 源自古英语 ceorfan（切割），与荷兰语 kerven 同源。

items.en: Old English ceorfan means to cut.
items.cn: 古英语 ceorfan 意为切割。

items.en: Middle English kerven keeps the cutting sense.
items.cn: 中古英语 kerven 保留切割义。

items.en: Carve settles into its modern spelling.
items.cn: 十五世纪 carve 定下现代拼写。

items.en: Carving the roast becomes a table ritual.
items.cn: 十七世纪切烤肉成为餐桌仪式。

items.en: Carving names both sculpture and craft.
items.cn: 现代兼指雕塑与手艺。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the carv- shape; the near-meaning group moves from woodwork to the dinner table.
note.cn: 形近组共享 carv- 形状；近义组从木工延伸到餐桌。

definition_zh: n. 小瀑布，瀑布群；瀑布状下垂物；v. 倾泻而下，层层落下
definition_en: a small waterfall or a series of them; to fall or flow in a continuous mass
core_image: 水沿着一级级岩石台阶层层跌落
scene: 溪水沿着一级级岩石台阶层叠落下，形成一道小瀑布。The stream cascades over the rock steps in a small waterfall.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：cascade 指小瀑布；句意是溪水沿石阶层层跌落。

senses.title: The falling water
senses.definition: a small waterfall, or water falling in stages
senses.definitionCN: 分成多级落下的小瀑布
senses.example: A narrow cascade fell into the pool.
senses.exampleCN: 一道细小的瀑布落入水潭。
senses.why: The word came from Italian cascare, to fall.
senses.whyCN: 该词来自意大利语 cascare，意为落下。

senses.title: Falling in a mass
senses.definition: to fall or hang in large amounts
senses.definitionCN: 大量地落下或垂落
senses.example: Loose papers cascaded from the shelf.
senses.exampleCN: 散落的纸张从架子上倾泻下来。
senses.why: The verb borrows the picture of falling water.
senses.whyCN: 动词借用落水的画面。

intro.en: Cascade comes from Italian cascata, from cascare, to fall, and reached English through French.
intro.cn: cascade 源自意大利语 cascata（cascare，落下），经法语进入英语。

items.en: Italian cascare means to fall.

items.en: Cascata names a falling of water.

items.en: French cascade names a small waterfall.

latinIntro.en: Latin cadere is to fall, aqua is water, and fluere is to flow.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 cadere 意为落下，aqua 意为水，fluere 意为流动。

latinEntries.exampleCN: cadere 产生 cascade 与 accident。
aqua 产生 aquatic 与 aquarium。
fluere 产生 fluid 与 fluent。

definition_zh: 现金；现款；兑现；赚钱
definition_en: money in the form of coins and notes, or to exchange a cheque for money
core_image: 钱箱里随时能拿出来的现钱
scene: 结账时收银员问怎么付款。She paid in cash and put the receipt in her bag.
sceneCN: 这里 cash 指「现金」（第 1 个义项：硬币和纸币形式的钱）；句意是她付了现金，把收据放进包里。

senses.title: Money in coins and notes
senses.definition: money in the form of coins and banknotes rather than cheques or cards
senses.definitionCN: 以硬币和纸币形式存在的钱，而非支票或银行卡
senses.example: He always carries some cash for the bus.
senses.exampleCN: 他总带些现金坐公交。
senses.why: The Latin source meant a money box, and the word shifted from the box to the ready money kept inside it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语源义是钱箱，词义从箱子转到箱子里随时可取的现钱。

senses.title: To exchange a cheque for money
senses.definition: to give or receive coins and notes in exchange for a cheque or other paper
senses.definitionCN: 用支票或其他票据换取硬币和纸币
senses.example: She cashed her salary cheque at the bank.
senses.exampleCN: 她在银行把工资支票兑成了现金。
senses.why: If cash is ready money, the verb names the act of turning paper into that ready money.
senses.whyCN: 既然 cash 是现钱，动词就指把票据变成现钱的动作。

senses.title: Funds available to a business
senses.definition: money that a company or person has available to spend at once
senses.definitionCN: 公司或个人当下可以动用的钱
senses.example: The firm ran out of cash in the spring.
senses.exampleCN: 公司在春天耗尽了资金。
senses.why: For a business, ready money on hand becomes a measure of health, so cash stands for available funds.
senses.whyCN: 对企业而言，手头的现钱成了经营健康的尺度，于是 cash 代指可动用资金。

intro.en: Cash goes back to a Latin word for a box, then to the money box and finally to the money inside.
intro.cn: cash 可追到拉丁语表示盒子的词，再经钱箱义，最后指箱子里的钱。

items.en: Capsa was a box or case, the container that held valuables.
items.cn: 拉丁语 capsa 指盒子或箱子，用来盛放贵重物品。

items.en: Italian cassa named a chest or money box in banking and trade.
items.cn: 意大利语 cassa 在金融和贸易中指钱柜或钱箱。

items.en: Middle French casse carried the money-box sense into northern Europe.
items.cn: 中古法语 casse 把钱箱义带到了北欧。

items.en: English cash first names a money box and soon the coin kept in it.
items.cn: 英语 cash 先指钱箱，很快又指箱里存放的硬币。

items.en: Banking adds the verb sense of cashing a cheque and the phrase cash flow.
items.cn: 银行业务又添上兑现支票的动词义和现金流这一说法。

note.en: The first group shares the money-box root, the second lists other words for money and payment.
note.cn: 第一组共享钱箱这一词根，第二组列出其他表示钱与支付的词。

entries.definition: a person who takes and pays out money
working without coins or notes
a record of money received and paid
the money used in a country
a piece of metal money
an amount paid or the act of paying
entries.definitionCN: 支付的款项或付款行为

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the money-box root, the fixed banking phrases and the short verb forms.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用钱箱词根、固定银行搭配，以及简短的动词形式。

normal.en: Cash and case share a Latin root meaning box, so cash is literally the money in the box.
normal.cn: cash 与 case 共享表示盒子的拉丁词根，cash 字面上就是箱子里的钱。

normal.en: A cashier is the person at the box, the one who takes and gives money.
normal.cn: cashier 就是守着钱箱的人，负责收钱和付钱。

normal.en: Cash flow pictures money moving in and out like water through a pipe.
normal.cn: cash flow 把钱的进出想象成水流过管道。

normal.en: Pay in cash is the everyday phrase that keeps the noun sense alive.
normal.cn: pay in cash 是让名词义保持活跃的日常说法。

normal.en: The third person cashes and the past cashed both keep the short -sh stem.
normal.cn: 三单 cashes 和过去式 cashed 都保留了短短的 -sh 词干。

abstract.en: Picture a wooden box overflowing with coins on a shop counter.
abstract.cn: 想象商店柜台上一个装满硬币的木箱。

abstract.en: Picture notes folded into a wallet before a trip.
abstract.cn: 想象出门前把纸币折好塞进钱包。

abstract.en: Picture a cheque turning into a stack of notes at the bank window.
abstract.cn: 想象一张支票在银行窗口变成一叠钞票。

examples.en: I have no cash with me today.
examples.cn: 我今天身上没带现金。

examples.en: Can you cash this cheque for me?
examples.cn: 你能帮我兑现这张支票吗？

examples.en: The shop only accepts cash.
examples.cn: 这家店只收现金。

dict_mnemonic.text: cash 读音接近「喀什」：想象在喀什的集市上掏出现金买东西。

root: 源自拉丁语 capsa（盒），经意大利语 cassa、中古法语 casse 进入英语，本指钱箱，后指箱中的现钱。

sensesIntro.en: A money box gives the ready money inside it, then the act of turning paper into that money, then the funds a business holds.
sensesIntro.cn: 钱箱先给出箱里的现钱，再给出把票据换成现钱的动作，最后给出企业持有的资金。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a box of ready money kept close at hand.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只装着现钱、随手可取的钱箱。

branches.en: The notes and coins in the box become the everyday cash sense.
branches.cn: 箱里的纸币和硬币成了日常的现金义。

branches.en: The verb turns a cheque into the contents of the box.
branches.cn: 动词义把支票变成箱子里的东西。

branches.en: For a company the box stands for the funds it can spend now.
branches.cn: 对公司来说，这只箱子代表它眼下能动用的资金。

branches.en: Both senses turn on the same contrast between paper claims and real money.
branches.cn: 两个义项都围绕票据与真钱之间的同一对照。

branches.en: Ready money is both what you carry and what a business measures.
branches.cn: 现钱既是随身携带的钱，也是企业衡量的指标。

intro.en: Cash grows a compact family through the -ier and -less endings and a few compounds.
intro.cn: cash 通过 -ier、-less 词尾和少量复合词形成一个小词族。

latinIntro.en: The ultimate source is Latin capsa, a box, which also underlies case and capsule.
latinIntro.cn: 最终源头是拉丁语 capsa（盒子），case 与 capsule 也出自这里。

items.example: Cash is king in small shops.

items.meaning: he or she exchanges for money
items.example: She cashes her cheque on Fridays.
He cashed the cheque at noon.
Cashing a cheque takes a minute.
The cashier counted the notes twice.
items.exampleCN: 收银员把钞票数了两遍。

items.example: The city is almost cashless now.
items.exampleCN: 这座城市如今几乎不用现金。

items.meaning: a book recording money paid and received
items.example: Every entry goes into the cashbook.

items.meaning: the movement of money in and out
items.exampleCN: 出售之后现金流好转了。

latinEntries.example: Capsa is the deep source of cash.
latinEntries.exampleCN: capsa 是 cash 的深层来源。

latinEntries.example: Cassa named the chest in old banks.
latinEntries.exampleCN: cassa 在老式银行里指钱柜。

definition_zh: n. 山羊绒，开司米；羊绒织物
definition_en: fine soft wool from the Kashmir goat; cloth made from this wool
core_image: 极细的浅色绒毛在指间柔软发亮
scene: 她围上一条浅灰色的羊绒围巾，柔软得像一层雾。She wrapped a pale grey cashmere scarf around her neck.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：cashmere 指山羊绒；句意是她围上柔软的羊绒围巾。

senses.title: The fine wool
senses.definition: soft fine wool taken from a kind of goat
senses.definitionCN: 取自一种山羊的细软绒毛
senses.example: The coat is lined with cashmere.
senses.exampleCN: 这件外套衬着羊绒。
senses.why: The fibre is named after Kashmir, where the goat is raised.
senses.whyCN: 这种纤维以产地克什米尔命名。

senses.title: The cloth
senses.definition: cloth woven from this wool
senses.definitionCN: 用这种绒毛织成的布料
senses.example: Cashmere feels warm without much weight.
senses.exampleCN: 羊绒保暖却不重。
senses.why: The material name spread to the garments made from it.
senses.whyCN: 材料名延伸到用它制成的衣物。

intro.en: Cashmere is an old spelling of Kashmir, the Himalayan region associated with the soft goat wool.
intro.cn: cashmere 是 Kashmir（克什米尔）的旧拼法，这一喜马拉雅地区以柔软山羊毛闻名。

items.en: Kashmir names a Himalayan valley.
items.cn: 克什米尔是喜马拉雅山谷之名。

items.en: Woven goat shawls reach Europe.
items.cn: 十八世纪山羊披肩传入欧洲。

items.en: English spells the cloth cashmere.
items.cn: 十九世纪英语把这种布拼作 cashmere。

items.en: Scottish mills weave fine cashmere.
items.cn: 十九世纪苏格兰织厂生产羊绒。

items.en: The name marks softness and expense.
items.cn: 现代该名代表柔软与昂贵。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the cash- sound; the near-meaning group sorts fine animal fibres.
note.cn: 形近组保留 cash- 音；近义组区分各类细动物纤维。

entries.definition: Coins and notes.
A hidden store of things.
A curved edible nut.
Fine hair from the Angora goat.
A soft shawl of fine wool.
Wool from a merino sheep.

normalIntro.en: Cashmere carries the name of Kashmir in every thread.
normalIntro.cn: cashmere 每一根线里都带着克什米尔的名字。

normal.en: Kashmir is a Himalayan valley.
normal.cn: 克什米尔是喜马拉雅山谷。

normal.en: Its goats grow very fine hair.
normal.cn: 那里的山羊长着极细的毛。

normal.en: English wrote the cloth as cashmere.
normal.cn: 英语把这布写作 cashmere。

normal.en: Soft shawls carried the name west.
normal.cn: 柔软的披肩把名字带到西方。

normal.en: Now the word means the fibre and the cloth.
normal.cn: 如今兼指纤维与布料。

abstract.en: A place folded into a fabric.
abstract.cn: 被折进布料里的一个地方。

abstract.en: Warmth measured in softness.
abstract.cn: 用柔软度衡量的温暖。

abstract.en: A goat mountain turned into a scarf.
abstract.cn: 一座山羊之山变成的围巾。

examples.en: This sweater is made of pure cashmere.
examples.cn: 这件毛衣是纯羊绒的。

examples.en: She folded the cashmere carefully into the drawer.
examples.cn: 她把羊绒衣物仔细叠进抽屉。

examples.en: The shop sells cashmeres from Scotland.
examples.cn: 这家店卖苏格兰产的羊绒制品。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「开司米」——开了丝一样的米白绒毛，就是羊绒。

root: 地名 Kashmir（克什米尔）→ 英语 cashmere

sensesIntro.en: The place gave its name to the fibre, and the fibre gave its name to the cloth.
sensesIntro.cn: 地名给了纤维名字，纤维又给了布料名字。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a handful of pale down softer than the light
core.cn: 核心意象：一把比光还柔的浅色绒毛

branches.en: A goat combed for winter down.
branches.cn: 为冬绒梳理的山羊。

branches.en: A scarf lighter than it looks.
branches.cn: 比看上去更轻的围巾。

branches.en: A shop window of soft grey folds.
branches.cn: 橱窗里柔软的灰褶。

branches.en: A coat that costs a month of wages.
branches.cn: 花掉一个月工资的外套。

branches.en: A valley worn on the shoulders.
branches.cn: 披在肩上的山谷。

intro.en: Cashmere is a place name; the list below adds words for wool, cloth and fibre.
intro.cn: cashmere 是地名；下面列出羊毛、布料、纤维词场的词缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin lana is wool, and texere is to weave.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 lana 意为羊毛，texere 意为编织。

latinEntries.exampleCN: lana 产生 lanolin 与 lanate。
texere 产生 textile 与 texture。
pilus 产生 pile 与 pilose。

definition_zh: 盒式磁带；暗盒；胶卷盒
definition_en: a small flat plastic case holding magnetic tape or film, used for recording sound or pictures
core_image: 一只扁平的小盒子，里面卷着长长的带子
scene: 她在阁楼里翻出一台旧录音机。The machine still played the cassette her father had recorded.
sceneCN: 这里 cassette 指「盒式磁带」（第 1 个义项：装着磁带的扁盒）；句意是这台机器还能播放她父亲录的那盘磁带。

senses.title: A case of magnetic tape
senses.definition: a small flat case containing magnetic tape that is played in a recorder
senses.definitionCN: 装着磁带、可放入录音机播放的扁平小盒
senses.example: He keeps his old cassettes in a shoebox.
senses.exampleCN: 他把旧磁带收在一个鞋盒里。
senses.why: The core image is a little box, and magnetic tape wound inside it is the use that made the word famous.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象就是一只小盒子，而卷在里面的磁带正是让这个词广为人知的用途。

senses.title: A lightproof film container
senses.definition: a lightproof case that holds photographic film and fits into a camera
senses.definitionCN: 装胶卷、可装入相机的防光小盒
senses.example: Load the cassette before you close the camera.
senses.exampleCN: 合上相机前先装好胶卷暗盒。
senses.why: This is the older photographic use: the same little case protects film from light instead of tape from dust.
senses.whyCN: 这是较早的摄影用法：同样的小盒子保护的是胶卷而不是磁带，防的是光而不是灰。

intro.en: Cassette is a French diminutive of a word for box, borrowed into English first for film and later for tape.
intro.cn: cassette 是法语中表示盒子的词的指小形式，英语先用它指胶卷盒，后指磁带盒。

items.en: Capsa meant a box, the same root that gives case and cash.
items.cn: 拉丁语 capsa 意为盒子，与 case、cash 同源。

items.en: Casse was a box, and cassette a little box, with the diminutive -ette.
items.cn: 法语 casse 指盒子，加指小词尾 -ette 后 cassette 就是小盒子。

items.en: English borrowed cassette for a small ornamental box.
items.cn: 英语在十八世纪借入 cassette，指小巧的装饰盒。

items.en: Photography applied the word to the lightproof case holding film.
items.cn: 十九世纪摄影术用该词指装胶卷的防光暗盒。

items.en: The tape recorder gave the word its most common modern meaning in the twentieth century.
items.cn: 二十世纪磁带录音机赋予该词今天最常见的含义。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the little-box root, while the meaning group gathers recording media.
note.cn: 形近组沿「小盒子」词根展开，近义组收录音载体。

entries.definition: a container for holding something
a very small tape cassette
a machine for playing tapes without a radio
entries.definitionCN: 不带收音功能的磁带播放机

entries.definition: a long thin strip coated for recording sound
entries.definitionCN: 涂有磁层用于录音的长带

entries.definition: a sealed case holding film or ink
entries.definitionCN: 装有胶卷或墨水的密封盒

entries.definition: a round holder that tape or film is wound on
entries.definitionCN: 缠绕磁带或胶卷的圆盘

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the little-box root, the -ette ending and the everyday player phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用小盒子词根、-ette 词尾以及日常播放机搭配。

normal.en: The ending -ette means little, as in cigarette and kitchenette, so a cassette is a little case.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ette 表示小，如 cigarette 和 kitchenette，所以 cassette 就是小盒子。

normal.en: Cassette and case share the Latin box root, which links the word to its shape.
normal.cn: cassette 与 case 共享拉丁语的盒子词根，这把词与外形连在一起。

normal.en: Cassette player and cassette recorder are the phrases that fix the tape sense.
normal.cn: cassette player 和 cassette recorder 是固定磁带义的搭配。

normal.en: Video cassette extends the same box to pictures as well as sound.
normal.cn: video cassette 把同一种盒子从声音扩展到画面。

normal.en: The plural cassettes simply adds an s, with no change of stress.
normal.cn: 复数 cassettes 只加一个 s，重音不变。

abstract.en: Picture a thin brown ribbon wound on two tiny wheels.
abstract.cn: 想象一条细细的棕色带子绕在两个小轮上。

abstract.en: Picture a finger pressing a stiff flap shut on a tape.
abstract.cn: 想象手指把磁带上硬硬的盖板按合。

abstract.en: Picture a dark room where film waits inside a sealed box.
abstract.cn: 想象暗室里胶卷待在密封盒中等待曝光。

examples.en: The cassette jammed inside the player.
examples.cn: 磁带卡在播放机里了。

examples.en: She labelled every cassette with a date.
examples.cn: 她给每盘磁带都标了日期。

examples.en: This camera takes a small film cassette.
examples.cn: 这台相机使用小号胶卷暗盒。

dict_mnemonic.text: cassette 的词尾 -ette 表示小，可以记成「小 case」：一只装着磁带的小盒子。

root: 源自法语 cassette（小盒子），由 casse（盒子）加指小词尾 -ette 构成，更早可追到拉丁语 capsa（盒）。

sensesIntro.en: A little box first holds ornaments, then film, then magnetic tape, and each use keeps the same shape.
sensesIntro.cn: 一只小盒子先装装饰品，再装胶卷，再装磁带，每种用途都保留同一外形。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small flat box with something wound inside.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只扁平小盒，里面卷着东西。

branches.en: Magnetic tape inside the box becomes the sound-recording sense.
branches.cn: 盒里的磁带成了录音义。

branches.en: Film inside the box becomes the photographic sense.
branches.cn: 盒里的胶卷成了摄影义。

branches.en: Both senses depend on the box keeping light and dust away from a sensitive strip.
branches.cn: 两个义项都依赖盒子替敏感的带子挡住光和灰尘。

branches.en: Player and recorder compounds keep this sense dominant today.
branches.cn: 播放机和录音机类复合词让这个义项在今天占据主导。

branches.en: The film sense now sounds old-fashioned but stays in camera manuals.
branches.cn: 胶卷义如今显得老旧，却仍留在相机说明书里。

intro.en: Cassette builds a thin family through compounds and the diminutive ending it already carries.
intro.cn: cassette 通过复合词和它本来就带的指小词尾形成一个小词族。

latinIntro.en: The word descends from Latin capsa, a box, through the French diminutive cassette.
latinIntro.cn: 该词经法语指小形式 cassette 上溯到拉丁语 capsa（盒子）。

items.meaning: a small tape or film case
items.example: The cassette is in the drawer.

items.exampleCN: 盒子里装了四十盘磁带。
这台磁带播放机还能用。

items.meaning: a machine that records on tapes
items.example: He bought a cheap cassette recorder.
items.exampleCN: 他买了台便宜的盒式录音机。
这台口述机用的是微型磁带。

items.meaning: a tape player without a radio

items.example: The case has a strong hinge.
items.exampleCN: 这只盒子有结实的合页。

latinEntries.example: Capsa is the deep root of cassette.
latinEntries.exampleCN: capsa 是 cassette 的深层词根。

latinEntries.example: French cassette added the sense of small.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 法语 cassette 加上了「小」的含义。

definition_zh: 投掷；投射；选派角色；演员阵容；铸造
definition_en: to throw something, to send light or a look in a direction, to choose actors for roles, or to pour metal into a shape
core_image: 把手中的东西用力甩出去
scene: 导演在排练厅里念出名单。The director cast two young actors in the leading roles.
sceneCN: 这里 cast 指「选派角色」（第 2 个义项：为戏剧挑选演员）；句意是导演让两位年轻演员出演主角。

pos.zh: 投掷；投射；选派角色；铸造

senses.title: To throw something
senses.definition: to throw something with force, especially so that it lands some distance away
senses.definitionCN: 用力把某物扔出去，尤指扔到较远处
senses.example: He cast the rope toward the shore.
senses.exampleCN: 他把绳子抛向岸边。
senses.why: The Norse source simply meant to throw, and that physical act remains the core of every later sense.
senses.whyCN: 古诺斯语源词本义就是扔，这个身体动作始终是后面所有义项的核心。

senses.title: To choose actors for roles
senses.definition: to select actors for the parts in a play or film
senses.definitionCN: 为戏剧或电影中的角色挑选演员
senses.example: They cast her as the queen.
senses.exampleCN: 他们让她演女王。
senses.why: Choosing an actor is pictured as throwing a person into a role, as if into a mould.
senses.whyCN: 选演员被想象成把人投进一个角色里，就像投进模具。

senses.title: The group of actors
senses.definition: all the actors who perform in a play or film
senses.definitionCN: 参与一部戏剧或电影演出的全体演员
senses.example: The whole cast came on stage for the applause.
senses.exampleCN: 全体演员上台接受掌声。
senses.why: Once people have been thrown into their parts, the collection of them takes the same noun.
senses.whyCN: 人一旦被投进各自的角色，这一群人就沿用了同一个名词。

senses.title: To send light or a look
senses.definition: to cause light, shadow or a glance to fall on something
senses.definitionCN: 使光、影或目光落到某物上
senses.example: The tall buildings cast long shadows.
senses.exampleCN: 高楼投下长长的影子。
senses.why: Light thrown from a source behaves like an object thrown forward, so the verb covers casting shadows.
senses.whyCN: 从光源甩出的光就像被抛出的物体，于是动词也覆盖了投下影子。

senses.title: To pour metal into a mould
senses.definition: to pour melted metal into a shaped container so that it hardens into an object
senses.definitionCN: 把熔化的金属倒入模具，冷却后成为物件
senses.example: The workers cast the bell in one piece.
senses.exampleCN: 工人们一次浇铸成了这口钟。
senses.why: Molten metal is literally thrown into a mould, keeping the old sense of a forceful pour.
senses.whyCN: 熔化的金属确实是被「倒抛」进模具，保留了用力倾倒的旧义。

intro.en: Cast came from Old Norse rather than Latin, and one physical sense of throwing spread into acting, light and metalwork.
intro.cn: cast 来自古诺斯语而非拉丁语，一个扔的动作向外扩展到表演、光线和金属加工。

items.en: A reconstructed verb for throwing or tossing underlies the Norse word.
items.cn: 一般认为有一个表示投掷的原始日耳曼语动词，是诺斯语词的来源。

items.en: Kasta meant to throw, and Norse settlers brought it into northern English.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 kasta 意为投掷，随北欧移民进入英格兰北部。

items.en: Casten spreads from throwing objects to throwing light, looks and dice.
items.cn: 中古英语 casten 从扔物体扩展到投光、投目光和掷骰子。

items.en: Metalwork gives the sense of pouring molten metal into a mould.
items.cn: 金属加工带来把熔融金属倒入模具的义项。

items.en: The theatre takes cast for the selection of actors and then for the whole company.
items.cn: 十七世纪戏剧界用 cast 指挑选演员，进而指整个演员班底。

items.en: Modern English keeps all these branches, from casting a vote to a plaster cast.
items.cn: 现代英语保留全部分支，从投票到石膏铸型。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the casting and throwing family, while the meaning group lists other throwing verbs.
note.cn: 形近组沿铸造与投掷词族展开，近义组列出其他表示扔的动词。

entries.definition: the act of shaping metal or choosing actors
a person who casts metal, or a small wheel
a person left alone after a shipwreck
entries.definitionCN: 海难后被弃在荒处的人

entries.definition: to send something through the air with the hand
to throw something with great force
to throw something quickly and carelessly

normalIntro.en: These hooks keep the single image of throwing and show how each phrase extends it.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子守住「扔」这一个画面，并展示每个搭配如何延伸它。

normal.en: Every sense begins with a hand throwing: a rope, a vote, a shadow, a role or molten metal.
normal.cn: 每个义项都从一只手扔出去开始：绳子、选票、影子、角色或熔融金属。

normal.en: Cast a vote pictures the ballot as a small object thrown into a box.
normal.cn: cast a vote 把选票想象成被扔进箱子的小物件。

normal.en: Cast a shadow keeps the image literal: light throws a dark shape onto the ground.
normal.cn: cast a shadow 保留字面画面：光把一块暗形扔到地面上。

normal.en: The past tense is cast, not casted, so the verb looks unchanged.
normal.cn: 过去式是 cast 而不是 casted，所以动词看起来没有变化。

normal.en: Casting covers both metal and actors because both involve pouring something into a prepared shape.
normal.cn: casting 同时指铸金属和选演员，因为两者都是把东西倒进预备好的形状里。

abstract.en: Picture a fisherman flinging a net in a wide arc.
abstract.cn: 想象渔夫把网甩出一个大弧。

abstract.en: Picture a director pointing at one actor in a crowded room.
abstract.cn: 想象导演在挤满人的房间里指向一位演员。

abstract.en: Picture sparks flying as hot metal fills a clay mould.
abstract.cn: 想象炽热的金属注入泥模时火星四溅。

examples.en: She cast the line far into the river.
examples.cn: 她把钓线远远抛进河里。

examples.en: The film has a strong cast.
examples.cn: 这部电影的演员阵容很强。

examples.en: The tree cast a cool shadow over the bench.
examples.cn: 那棵树在长椅上投下一片凉影。

dict_mnemonic.text: cast 的核心动作就是「扔」：把绳子扔出去，把票扔进箱，把演员扔进角色，把铁水扔进模具。

root: 源自古诺斯语 kasta（投掷），属日耳曼语词，无拉丁语祖先；由「扔」这一动作扩展出投射、选角与铸造诸义。

sensesIntro.en: One throwing gesture gives the rope, the vote, the shadow, the actor and the molten metal.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个投掷动作先后给出绳子、选票、影子、演员和熔融金属。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand sending something forward through the air.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把东西向前甩到空中。

branches.en: The literal throw stays in fishing, dice and ropes.
branches.cn: 字面的扔保留在钓鱼、掷骰和抛绳中。

branches.en: Light thrown from a source lays a shadow down.
branches.cn: 从光源甩出的光把影子放倒在地上。

branches.en: Actors are thrown into parts, and the group of them becomes the cast.
branches.cn: 演员被投进角色，这一群人就成为演员阵容。

branches.en: Molten metal is poured into a mould and hardens into a cast object.
branches.cn: 熔融金属被倒入模具，凝固成铸件。

branches.en: Both keep the force of a deliberate, aimed pour or toss.
branches.cn: 两者都保留了有目标、有力度的倾倒或抛掷感。

intro.en: Cast builds compounds and agent nouns rather than taking classical affixes.
intro.cn: cast 主要构成复合词和表施动者的名词，不常接古典词缀。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic and has no Latin ancestor, so no Latin cognates are listed.
latinIntro.cn: 该词属日耳曼语，没有拉丁语祖先，因此不列拉丁同源词。

items.example: They cast the net at dawn.

items.meaning: the act of shaping or selecting
a metal worker or a small wheel
items.example: The caster lifted the hot mould.
items.exampleCN: 铸工抬起了滚烫的模具。

items.meaning: a statement about what will happen
a hard iron made by casting
items.example: The pan is made of cast iron.

definition_zh: 城堡；堡垒；车（国际象棋）
definition_en: a large strong building with thick walls and towers, built to defend a place, or the rook in chess
core_image: 建在高处的石墙与塔楼
scene: 旅行团沿着山路走到一座石砌建筑前。The guide explained how the castle had survived three sieges.
sceneCN: 这里 castle 指「城堡」（第 1 个义项：带厚墙与塔楼的防御建筑）；句意是导游讲解这座城堡如何熬过三次围攻。

senses.title: A fortified stone building
senses.definition: a large building with thick walls, towers and often a moat, built to resist attack
senses.definitionCN: 带厚墙、塔楼，常有护城河，为抵御进攻而建的大型建筑
senses.example: The castle stands on a hill above the town.
senses.exampleCN: 城堡坐落在小镇上方的山丘上。
senses.why: The Latin source was a small fort, and the stone walls and towers grew out of that defensive core.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语源词指小要塞，石墙与塔楼正是从这一防御核心长出来的。

senses.title: The rook in chess
senses.definition: one of the two pieces in chess shaped like a tower, moving in straight lines
senses.definitionCN: 国际象棋中形似塔楼、沿直线行走的两个棋子之一
senses.example: He moved his castle to the open file.
senses.exampleCN: 他把车移到开放线上。
senses.why: The chess piece was carved as a turret, so the tower shape lent its name to the piece.
senses.whyCN: 这枚棋子被雕成小塔楼，于是塔楼的名称就借给了它。

intro.en: Castle descends from a Latin diminutive of a word for fort, and the chess piece borrowed its tower shape.
intro.cn: castle 源自拉丁语中表示要塞的词的指小形式，棋子则借用了它的塔楼外形。

items.en: Castrum meant a fortified camp, and its plural castra named a fort.
items.cn: 拉丁语 castrum 指设防营地，复数 castra 指要塞。

items.en: Castellum, a little fort, is the diminutive that leads to the English word.
items.cn: 指小形式 castellum 意为小要塞，是通向英语词的直接来源。

items.en: Castel enters Old English through Latin and Anglo-Norman French.
items.cn: castel 经拉丁语和盎格鲁诺曼法语进入古英语。

items.en: Castle settles as the word for a nobleman's fortified stone home.
items.cn: 中古英语时期，castle 固定指贵族设防的石砌宅邸。

items.en: The word also names the tower-shaped rook and the sandcastle on the beach.
items.cn: 现代英语中，它也指塔楼形的国际象棋车和沙滩上的沙堡。

note.en: The look-alike group stays with the Latin fort root, and the meaning group gathers other strongholds.
note.cn: 形近组留在拉丁语要塞词根内，近义组收其他坚固据点。

entries.definition: the governor of a castle
built with battlements like a castle
a large French country house or castle
a large strong building used for defence
entries.definitionCN: 用于防御的大型坚固建筑

entries.definition: the large official home of a ruler
a tall narrow building or part of one
entries.definitionCN: 高而窄的建筑物或其一部分

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the Latin fort root, the chess shape and the sandcastle image.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用拉丁语要塞词根、棋子的形状和沙堡的画面。

normal.en: The Latin root castrum, a fort, also hides in castellum, the little fort behind castle.
normal.cn: 拉丁语词根 castrum（要塞）也藏在 castellum 里，后者正是 castle 背后的「小要塞」。

normal.en: The chess castle is simply a tower carved in wood or plastic.
normal.cn: 国际象棋里的车不过是一座用木头或塑料雕成的塔楼。

normal.en: Sand castle keeps the word alive on every beach, with walls and towers in miniature.
normal.cn: sand castle 让这个词活在每片沙滩上，用缩小版的墙和塔。

normal.en: Castle in the air means a plan with no foundation, like a castle built on nothing.
normal.cn: castle in the air 指没有根基的计划，就像建在虚空里的城堡。

normal.en: Only the plural castles is needed, since the noun has no verb use here.
normal.cn: 这里只需复数 castles，因为该名词在此没有动词用法。

abstract.en: Picture a grey wall rising above a moat at sunset.
abstract.cn: 想象日落时一道灰墙从护城河上方升起。

abstract.en: Picture a wooden tower sliding across a chessboard.
abstract.cn: 想象一座木塔在棋盘上滑动。

abstract.en: Picture a child patting wet sand into a tiny turret.
abstract.cn: 想象孩子把湿沙拍成一座小塔。

examples.en: The old castle is open to visitors in summer.
examples.cn: 这座古堡夏天对游客开放。

examples.en: They built a sand castle near the water.
examples.cn: 他们在水边堆了一座沙堡。

examples.en: His plan was a castle in the air.
examples.cn: 他的计划只是空中楼阁。

dict_mnemonic.text: castle 可以想成「卡住」的石头：一层层石头卡在一起，垒成高墙和塔楼。

root: 源自拉丁语 castellum（小要塞），是 castrum（设防营地）的指小形式，经古英语 castel 进入现代拼写。

sensesIntro.en: A small Latin fort grows into a stone home with towers, and its tower shape then names the chess piece.
sensesIntro.cn: 拉丁语的小要塞长成带塔楼的石砌宅邸，塔楼外形又给国际象棋的棋子命了名。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: thick stone walls and towers on high ground.
core.cn: 核心意象：高地上的厚石墙与塔楼。

branches.en: Defence stays the first job of the building through the Middle Ages.
branches.cn: 在整个中世纪，防御始终是这座建筑的首要功能。

branches.en: The tower silhouette is copied onto the chessboard.
branches.cn: 塔楼的轮廓被复制到了棋盘上。

branches.en: Later castles become grand homes as much as forts.
branches.cn: 后来的城堡既是堡垒，也成为气派的宅邸。

branches.en: Both senses keep the tower as their shared outline.
branches.cn: 两个义项都以塔楼作为共同轮廓。

branches.en: The sandcastle is a playful miniature of the same walls.
branches.cn: 沙堡就是同样城墙的玩闹缩微版。

intro.en: Castle forms a small family through the -an and -ated endings and a few compounds.
intro.cn: castle 通过 -an、-ated 词尾和少量复合词形成一个小词族。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base castrum, a fort, also appears in place names such as Chester and Lancaster.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语词基 castrum（要塞）也出现在 Chester、Lancaster 等地名中。

items.example: The valley is full of castles.
items.exampleCN: 这条山谷里到处是城堡。

items.example: The castellan met them at the gate.
items.exampleCN: 城堡主在大门迎接他们。

items.example: The house has a castellated roof.
items.exampleCN: 这所房子有城堡式的屋顶。

items.example: The tide washed the sandcastle away.
They stayed in a chateau in the Loire.
items.exampleCN: 他们住在卢瓦尔河畔的一座庄园里。

items.example: Castrum survives in many place names.
items.exampleCN: castrum 存留在许多地名中。

items.example: Castellum is the direct source of castle.
items.exampleCN: castellum 是 castle 的直接来源。

latinEntries.exampleCN: castrum 指罗马军队的营寨。

definition_zh: 随意的；非正式的；漫不经心的；临时的
definition_en: relaxed and informal in manner or dress, not showing much care, or happening by chance and without a plan
core_image: 没有事先安排、随手就来的样子
scene: 公司周五允许员工不穿西装。On Fridays the office has a casual dress code.
sceneCN: 这里 casual 指「随意的」（第 1 个义项：不正式、轻松的穿着方式）；句意是每逢周五，办公室执行休闲着装规定。

pos.zh: 随意的；非正式的；漫不经心的；临时的

senses.title: Relaxed and informal
senses.definition: relaxed in style, not formal or planned, especially of clothes or gatherings
senses.definitionCN: 风格轻松，不正式或没有安排，尤指衣着或聚会
senses.example: He wore casual clothes to the dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 他穿着休闲服去参加晚宴。
senses.why: What happens by chance has no ceremony, so dress without ceremony becomes casual dress.
senses.whyCN: 偶然发生的事没有仪式感，于是不带仪式感的穿着就成了 casual 的穿着。

senses.title: Showing little care
senses.definition: done without attention or serious thought, sometimes causing harm
senses.definitionCN: 做事不加注意或不认真思考，有时造成损害
senses.example: A casual remark hurt her feelings.
senses.exampleCN: 一句随口的话伤了她的心。
senses.why: An unplanned act is also an unconsidered one, so the chance sense shades into carelessness.
senses.whyCN: 没有计划的行为也往往没有经过思考，于是偶然义渐渐带上马虎义。

senses.title: Temporary or occasional
senses.definition: employed for a short time or happening at irregular intervals
senses.definitionCN: 短期受雇的，或间隔不固定地发生的
senses.example: The hotel hires casual staff in summer.
senses.exampleCN: 这家酒店夏天雇临时工。
senses.why: Work that comes by chance rather than by contract is casual work, done by casual workers.
senses.whyCN: 靠机会而非合同来的工作就是临时工作，由临时工来做。

intro.en: Casual goes back to the Latin word for a fall or event, so its first meaning is simply what happens by chance.
intro.cn: casual 可追到拉丁语中表示落下或事件的词，所以它最初的意思就是偶然发生的。

items.en: Casus meant a fall or an event, from cadere, to fall.
items.cn: 拉丁语 casus 意为落下或事件，源自动词 cadere（落下）。

items.en: Casualis described whatever happened by chance rather than by design.
items.cn: casualis 形容偶然发生、并非有意安排的事。

items.en: Casuel carried the chance sense into medieval French and then into English.
items.cn: 古法语 casuel 把偶然义带入中古法语，再进入英语。

items.en: English casual first means happening by chance, without plan or regularity.
items.cn: 英语 casual 最初指偶然发生、没有计划或规律。

items.en: The word extends to informal dress, relaxed manners and short-term work.
items.cn: 此后词义扩展到休闲衣着、随便的举止和短期工作。

items.en: Casual Friday and casual wear now fix the relaxed sense in everyday use.
items.cn: casual Friday 与 casual wear 让轻松义在日常用语中固定下来。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the chance root through its adverbs and nouns, while the meaning group offers nearby adjectives.
note.cn: 形近组沿偶然这一词根经副词与名词展开，近义组给出相近的形容词。

entries.definition: in a relaxed or careless way
the quality of being informal
a person killed or injured in an accident or war
entries.definitionCN: 在事故或战争中死伤的人

entries.definition: relaxed and without strict rules
calm and not worried
happening by chance, not on purpose

normalIntro.en: These hooks tie casual to the event root, to the -ly adverb and to the everyday dress phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子把 casual 与事件词根、-ly 副词和日常着装搭配连起来。

normal.en: Casual shares its root with case: both come from casus, an event that falls out.
normal.cn: casual 与 case 同根，都来自 casus，即落下来的事件。

normal.en: Casualty began as a chance event and now means a person hurt by one.
normal.cn: casualty 最初指偶然事件，现在指在事件中受伤的人。

normal.en: Casual clothes and casual Friday keep the informal sense visible every week.
normal.cn: casual clothes 和 casual Friday 每周都在提醒非正式这一含义。

normal.en: The -ly adverb casually simply adds the manner sense to the adjective.
normal.cn: 副词 casually 只是在形容词上加了方式义。

normal.en: More casual and most casual take a helper word because the adjective is long.
normal.cn: 因为词形较长，比较级和最高级用 more 与 most 来构成。

abstract.en: Picture a man in sandals at a formal dinner, completely at ease.
abstract.cn: 想象一位穿凉鞋出席正式晚宴却毫不拘束的男子。

abstract.en: Picture a remark tossed out without thinking, then landing hard.
abstract.cn: 想象一句没经思考就抛出的话，落地却很重。

abstract.en: Picture a worker hired for one busy weekend and paid by the day.
abstract.cn: 想象一个只在忙碌周末受雇、按天结钱的工人。

examples.en: The party was casual, so nobody dressed up.
examples.cn: 聚会很随意，所以没人特意打扮。

examples.en: He made a casual remark about the weather.
examples.cn: 他随口说了句天气的话。

examples.en: The factory takes on casual workers at harvest time.
examples.cn: 工厂在收获季节雇临时工。

dict_mnemonic.text: casual 里有 case：把生活看成一件件偶然落下的 case，穿着随意、说话随口都叫 casual。

root: 源自拉丁语 casualis（偶然的），再由 casus（落下、事件）派生，与 case 同根。

sensesIntro.en: What happens by chance needs no ceremony, no care and no long contract, so one root yields informality, carelessness and temporary work.
sensesIntro.cn: 偶然发生的事既不需要仪式，也不需要用心和长期合同，于是一个词根给出随意、马虎和临时这三层意思。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something that simply falls out without plan.
core.cn: 核心意象：没有计划、自己落下来的事。

branches.en: Chance work is work without a long agreement.
branches.cn: 偶然来的工作就是没有长期约定的工作。

branches.en: An occasion without ceremony lets clothes become casual.
branches.cn: 不带仪式的场合格调，让穿着也变得休闲。

branches.en: A remark made without thought is the careless side of the same root.
branches.cn: 未经思考的话就是同一词根的马虎一面。

branches.en: Both senses lack preparation, one in style and one in attention.
branches.cn: 两个义项都缺准备，一个缺在风格，一个缺在注意力。

branches.en: Relaxed dress and short-term work both sit outside formal rules.
branches.cn: 休闲着装与短期工作都处在正式规则之外。

intro.en: Casual takes the -ly and -ness endings and one old noun, casualty, that drifted far from its root.
intro.cn: casual 接 -ly 与 -ness 词尾，另有一个离开词根很远的旧名词 casualty。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin casualis, from casus, the same event word behind case and occasion.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是拉丁语 casualis，出自 casus，与 case、occasion 共享同一个事件词。

items.example: The casualness of the office surprised him.
items.exampleCN: 办公室的随意气氛让他吃惊。

items.meaning: a day when informal dress is allowed
items.meaningCN: 允许穿休闲装的工作日
items.exampleCN: 休闲星期五是上个月开始的。

items.example: Casualis is the Latin source of casual.
items.exampleCN: casualis 是 casual 的拉丁语来源。
casus 也是英语 case 的来源。

latinEntries.exampleCN: casualis 形容没有计划的事件。

latinEntries.example: Casus lies behind case and casual.
latinEntries.exampleCN: casus 是 case 与 casual 的源头。

definition_zh: n. 伤亡人员，死伤者；受害者；（英式）急诊室
definition_en: a person killed or injured in an accident or war; someone or something harmed by an event
core_image: 事故现场被抬上担架的人
scene: 事故发生后，唯一的伤亡者被立即送往医院。The only casualty of the crash was taken to hospital at once.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：casualty 指伤亡人员；句意是事故中唯一的伤者被立刻送医。

pos.zh: 伤亡人员；受害者；急诊室

senses.title: A person hurt or killed
senses.definition: someone killed or injured in an accident or fighting
senses.definitionCN: 在事故或战斗中死亡或受伤的人
senses.example: The rescue team counted the casualties.
senses.exampleCN: 救援队清点了伤亡人数。
senses.why: The word first meant what happens by chance, then a chance injury.
senses.whyCN: 该词原指偶然发生之事，后指意外伤害。

senses.title: Someone harmed by events
senses.definition: a person or thing damaged by a change or decision
senses.definitionCN: 因变化或决定而受损的人或事物
senses.example: Small shops were the first casualty of the new road.
senses.exampleCN: 小店是新道路的首批受害者。
senses.why: The sense widened from battle to any loss.
senses.whyCN: 词义从战场扩展到任何损失。

senses.title: The hospital unit
senses.definition: the emergency department of a hospital in British use
senses.definitionCN: 英式英语中指医院急诊部
senses.example: They rushed him to casualty.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把他紧急送到急诊室。
senses.why: British hospitals named the unit for the cases it receives.
senses.whyCN: 英国医院按接收的病例给该科室命名。

intro.en: Casualty comes from Latin casualis, by chance, through French, and first meant a chance event.
intro.cn: casualty 经法语源自拉丁语 casualis（偶然的），最初指偶然事件。

items.en: Latin casualis means by chance.
items.cn: 拉丁语 casualis 意为偶然。

items.en: French casualte names a chance event.
items.cn: 十四世纪法语 casualte 指偶然事件。

items.en: English casualty means an accident.
items.cn: 十五世纪英语指意外事故。

items.en: The word shifts to the hurt and the dead.
items.cn: 十七世纪词义转向伤者与死者。

items.en: British hospitals open casualty wards.
items.cn: 十九世纪英国医院设急诊科。

normalIntro.cn: casualty 是偶然事件留下的后果。

normal.en: Casualis meant by chance.
normal.cn: casualis 意为偶然。

normal.en: A casualty was first an accident.

normal.en: War moved it to the hurt and dead.

normal.en: Shoppers can be casualties of a new road.

abstract.en: A list that grows shorter than the crowd.

sensesIntro.cn: 偶然造出这个词，战争磨利了它，医院又给了它一间房。

branches.en: A list read aloud after a battle.

branches.en: An ambulance at the roadside.

branches.en: A shop closing beside a new road.

branches.cn: 急诊室里的一夜班。

latinIntro.en: Latin casus is a fall or chance, and nocere is to harm.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 casus 意为坠落或偶然，nocere 意为伤害。

nocere 产生 innocent 与 noxious。
victima 产生 victim 与 victimise。

definition_zh: n. 大灾难，剧变；（地质）灾变
definition_en: a violent event that causes great change, such as a flood, an earthquake or a war
core_image: 洪水瞬间吞没整片平原
scene: 洪水在一夜之间吞没平原，这场灾变改写了整片地貌。The flood that swallowed the plain was a cataclysm no map could ignore.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：cataclysm 指大灾变；句意是洪水一夜吞没平原，改变了地貌。

senses.title: The great disaster
senses.definition: a sudden violent event that changes the earth or a society
senses.definitionCN: 突然而猛烈、改变地貌或社会的事件
senses.example: The eruption was a cataclysm for the island.
senses.exampleCN: 那次喷发对这座岛是场大灾变。
senses.why: Greek kataklysmos meant a flood washing everything away.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 kataklysmos 指冲走一切的洪水。

senses.title: A violent change
senses.definition: a sudden great change in politics or society
senses.definitionCN: 政治或社会中的突然巨变
senses.example: The revolution was a cataclysm for the old order.
senses.exampleCN: 这场革命对旧秩序是场剧变。
senses.why: The flood image widened to any sweeping change.
senses.whyCN: 洪水意象扩展到任何席卷性的变化。

intro.en: Cataclysm comes from Greek kataklysmos, a flood, built from kata, down, and klyzein, to wash.
intro.cn: cataclysm 源自希腊语 kataklysmos（洪水），由 kata（向下）与 klyzein（冲刷）构成。

items.en: Greek kata means down.
items.cn: 希腊语 kata 意为向下。

items.en: Greek klyzein means to wash.
items.cn: 希腊语 klyzein 意为冲刷。

items.en: Kataklysmos names a great flood.
items.cn: kataklysmos 指大洪水。

items.en: English cataclysm names a deluge.
items.cn: 十七世纪英语指大洪水。

items.en: Geology uses it for earth-shaking events.
items.cn: 十九世纪地质学用它指撼动大地的事件。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the cata- opening; the near-meaning group ranks disasters by scale.
note.cn: 形近组共享 cata- 开头；近义组按规模排列灾难。

normalIntro.en: A cataclysm is a flood that refuses to stay in the river.
normalIntro.cn: cataclysm 是一场不肯待在河里的洪水。

normal.en: Kata means down.
normal.cn: kata 意为向下。

normal.en: Klyzein means to wash.
normal.cn: klyzein 意为冲刷。

normal.en: Together they name a great flood.
normal.cn: 合起来指大洪水。

normal.en: Geology borrowed it for the shaking earth.
normal.cn: 地质学借它指大地震动。

normal.en: Politics borrowed it for sudden change.
normal.cn: 政治借它指突变。

abstract.en: A river deciding to become a sea.
abstract.cn: 一条决定变成海的河。

abstract.en: History rewritten in one night.
abstract.cn: 一夜之间被改写的历史。

abstract.en: The moment after which maps differ.
abstract.cn: 之后地图都不同的那一刻。

examples.en: The story describes a cataclysm that drowned the coast.
examples.cn: 这个故事描述了一场淹没海岸的大灾变。

examples.en: War was the cataclysm that ended the old empire.
examples.cn: 战争是终结旧帝国的那场剧变。

examples.en: Scientists study cataclysms in the rock record.
examples.cn: 科学家在岩石记录中研究古代灾变。

sensesIntro.en: The word began as water and grew to cover any flood of change.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从水开始，扩展到任何变化的洪水。

core.cn: 核心意象：夜里横过平原的一道水墙

branches.en: A coast disappearing under grey water.

latinIntro.en: Greek kata is down, klyzein is to wash, and Latin clades is a disaster.

definition_zh: n. 地下墓穴，地下墓道
definition_en: an underground gallery with burial places cut into its walls
core_image: 幽暗的地下长廊两侧排满墓龛
scene: 火把照亮地下长廊，两侧石壁上凿满一层层的墓龛。Torchlight lit the catacomb, where rows of graves were cut into the walls.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：catacomb 指地下墓穴；句意是火把照亮长廊，两侧凿满墓龛。

senses.title: The underground gallery
senses.definition: an underground passage used for burials
senses.definitionCN: 用于埋葬的地下通道
senses.example: The catacomb runs for miles under the city.
senses.exampleCN: 这条墓道在城市下方延伸数英里。
senses.why: The name may join Greek kata, down, with Latin cumba, a hollow.
senses.whyCN: 该名可能由希腊语 kata（向下）与拉丁语 cumba（凹槽）构成。

senses.title: The burial place as a whole
senses.definition: a whole network of such passages and graves
senses.definitionCN: 这类通道与墓穴构成的整体
senses.example: Visitors are not allowed into the oldest catacomb.
senses.exampleCN: 游客不得进入最古老的地下墓群。
senses.why: The plural often names the whole complex.
senses.whyCN: 复数形式常指整个墓群。

intro.en: Catacomb probably joins Greek kata, down, with Latin cumba, a hollow, and first named the tunnels near Rome.

items.en: The tunnels around Rome gain the name.

normalIntro.cn: catacomb 是建在活人之城下方的死者之城。

normal.en: Kata means down.

normal.en: Cumba means a hollow.

normal.en: Soft rock could be dug for miles.

normal.en: Graves were cut into the walls.

abstract.cn: 街下的一条街，留给离开的人。

abstract.en: Light carried carefully into stone.
abstract.cn: 被小心带进石头里的光。

abstract.en: A quiet city with no doors.

examples.en: Early Christians met in the catacombs outside Rome.

examples.en: Workers found a catacomb beneath the new car park.
examples.cn: 工人在新停车场下方发现了一处地下墓穴。

definition_zh: 目录；目录册；一系列；编入目录
definition_en: a book or list that names things in order, especially goods or library holdings, or to enter items into such a list
core_image: 一页页排好的条目，像账簿一样整齐
scene: 拍卖行整理本季的拍品。The auction house printed a thick catalogue of paintings.
sceneCN: 这里 catalogue 指「目录册」（第 1 个义项：装订成册的条目清单）；句意是拍卖行印了一本厚厚的画作目录。

senses.title: A book listing items
senses.definition: a printed book or document that lists goods, works of art or books in order
senses.definitionCN: 按顺序列出商品、艺术品或书籍的印刷册子或文件
senses.example: The gallery sent me its new catalogue.
senses.exampleCN: 画廊给我寄来了新目录。
senses.why: The Greek list word was first spoken, then written, and finally bound as a book.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语的清单词先从口头念出，再写下来，最后装订成册。

senses.title: A long series of events
senses.definition: a continuous series of things, especially unpleasant ones, that seem to be counted off
senses.definitionCN: 连续发生的一串事情，尤指像是被逐项数出的不快之事
senses.example: The year was a catalogue of mistakes.
senses.exampleCN: 那一年是一连串错误的集合。
senses.why: If a catalogue counts items, then a year full of faults can itself be read as a catalogue.
senses.whyCN: 既然目录是逐项清点，那么满是过失的一年本身也能读成一份目录。

senses.title: To enter items in a list
senses.definition: to record objects or works in an ordered list, often with numbers and descriptions
senses.definitionCN: 把物品或作品记入有序清单，常附编号与说明
senses.example: They catalogued the letters before storing them.
senses.exampleCN: 他们先把信件编目，然后才归档。
senses.why: To catalogue is to do the counting work that produces a catalogue.
senses.whyCN: 编目就是做那份清点工作，从而产生一份目录。

intro.en: Catalogue keeps the French spelling of the Greek list word, and its -ue ending still marks the British form today.
intro.cn: catalogue 保留了希腊语清单词的法语拼写，结尾的 -ue 至今是英式拼写的标志。

items.en: Katalogos meant a list or register, from kata and legein, to say or count.
items.cn: 希腊语 katalogos 意为清单或名录，由 kata 与 legein（说、点数）构成。

items.en: Catalogus carried the word into the written culture of the Roman world.
items.cn: 拉丁语 catalogus 把该词带入罗马世界的书写文化。

items.en: Catalogue gave English the -ue spelling that British usage still prefers.
items.cn: 法语 catalogue 给英语留下了英式用法偏爱的 -ue 拼写。

items.en: Catalogue is recorded as a list of names or books arranged for reference.
items.cn: 十五世纪英语中，catalogue 已有按序排列名称或书籍的记录。

items.en: Art dealers and libraries make the printed catalogue a standard tool.
items.cn: 十九世纪艺术品商人与图书馆把印刷目录变成标准工具。

items.en: The phrase a catalogue of disasters fixes the figurative series sense.
items.cn: 短语 a catalogue of disasters 固定了比喻性的「一连串」义。

note.en: The look-alike group stays with the -ue spelling and its derivatives, and the meaning group gives other records.
note.cn: 形近组留在 -ue 拼写及其派生词内，近义组给出其他记录形式。
