normal.cn: a catalogue of disasters 就是把一整年的麻烦逐条念出来。

normal.en: Catalogue numbers give each listed work a small address of its own.
normal.cn: 目录编号给每件列出的作品一个小地址。

abstract.en: Picture a thick book with gilt numbers down the spine.
abstract.cn: 想象一本厚书，书脊上印着烫金编号。

abstract.en: Picture an auctioneer tapping a page of listed paintings.
abstract.cn: 想象拍卖师敲着写满画作的那一页。

abstract.en: Picture a shelf of boxes, each labelled with a neat number.
abstract.cn: 想象一整排箱子，每只都标着整齐的编号。

examples.en: The catalogue lists every piece in the show.
examples.cn: 目录列出了展览中的每件作品。

examples.en: She found the price in the auction catalogue.
examples.cn: 她在拍卖目录里找到了价格。

examples.en: The collection was catalogued over ten years.
examples.cn: 这批藏品用了十年时间编目。

dict_mnemonic.text: catalogue 里的 log 是记录：把展品一件件记进本子，就成了一本目录册。

root: 与 catalog 同源，出自希腊语 katalogos（清单），经拉丁语 catalogus 与法语 catalogue 进入英语，-ue 为法式拼写残留。

sensesIntro.en: A spoken counting-off becomes a printed book, then a year of misfortunes, while the verb names the counting itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 口头的逐项点数变成印刷册子，再变成一年的不幸，而动词则指点数这个动作本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: numbered entries standing in neat rows.
core.cn: 核心意象：编了号、排成整齐行列的条目。

branches.en: The written list is bound and sold as a catalogue.
branches.cn: 写下的清单被装订起来，作为目录册出售。

branches.en: A run of bad events is counted off like entries.
branches.cn: 一连串坏事像条目一样被逐项数出。

branches.en: The verb performs the counting that fills the book.
branches.cn: 动词义执行填入册子的清点工作。

branches.en: Book and action are two sides of the same ordered record.
branches.cn: 册子与动作是同一份有序记录的两面。

branches.en: Both senses rely on the feeling of a long, orderly series.
branches.cn: 两个义项都依赖「长而有序的一串」这种感觉。

intro.en: Catalogue forms -er and -ing nouns and keeps the French -ue in every British spelling.
intro.cn: catalogue 构成 -er 与 -ing 名词，英式拼写始终保留法语式 -ue。

latinIntro.en: Latin catalogus kept the Greek list word, which French later reshaped as catalogue.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 catalogus 保留了希腊语清单词，法语后来把它改写成 catalogue。

items.example: The cataloguer noted a missing page.
items.exampleCN: 编目员注意到缺了一页。

items.meaning: the same word in American English

items.exampleCN: catalogus 见于中世纪图书馆。

latinEntries.example: Catalogus is the Latin bridge to English.
latinEntries.exampleCN: catalogus 是通向英语的拉丁语桥梁。

definition_zh: 催化作用；催化；促成变化的中介力量
definition_en: the process by which a substance speeds up a reaction while itself remaining unchanged
core_image: 一条陡峭的山路旁多出一条平缓隧道，走路的人还是那些人，路却通了
scene: 一条陡峭的山路旁多出一条平缓隧道，走路的人还是那些人，路却通了。A trace of platinum speeds up the reaction through catalysis.
sceneCN: 这里 catalysis 指催化剂加快反应而自身不被消耗的作用（第 1 个义项：降低反应阻力、加快反应速度的过程）；句意：微量铂通过催化作用加快了反应。图中可辨识物件：陡坡、隧道口、行走的人、路面标线。

senses.title: Speeding a reaction without being consumed
senses.titleCN: 不消耗自身而加快反应
senses.definition: the chemical process in which a substance lowers the barrier to a reaction and is recovered unchanged
senses.definitionCN: 某种物质降低反应阻力、自身却在反应后原样回收的化学过程
senses.example: A trace of platinum speeds up the reaction through catalysis.
senses.exampleCN: 微量铂通过催化作用加快了反应。
senses.why: the Greek word meant a loosening or dissolving, and chemistry borrowed that image for the removal of a barrier that held the reaction back.
senses.whyCN: 这个希腊词原意是「松开、化解」，化学借这个意象表示移除挡住反应的那道障碍。

senses.title: Catalysis inside a living cell
senses.definition: the same speeding-up performed by enzymes on biological molecules
senses.definitionCN: 由酶对生物分子执行的同类加速作用
senses.example: Enzyme catalysis lets a cell break down sugar at body temperature.
senses.exampleCN: 酶催化让细胞在体温下分解糖。
senses.why: enzymes do exactly what metal catalysts do, only more precisely, so biology uses the same noun for the process.
senses.whyCN: 酶做的事与金属催化剂完全相同，只是更精准，因此生物学用同一个名词指这一过程。

senses.title: Catalysis as an industrial process
senses.definition: the use of catalysts on a plant scale to make fuels, fertiliser or plastics
senses.definitionCN: 在工厂规模上使用催化剂来生产燃料、肥料或塑料
senses.example: Industrial catalysis turns most of the world's ammonia into fertiliser.
senses.exampleCN: 工业催化把世界上大部分氨变成肥料。
senses.why: when the process leaves the flask for a reactor, the noun shifts from a mechanism to a production method.
senses.whyCN: 当这一过程离开烧瓶进入反应器，这个名词便从机理转为生产方法。

senses.title: The field that studies catalysts
senses.titleCN: 研究催化剂的学科领域
senses.definition: the branch of chemistry concerned with how catalysts work and how to design them
senses.definitionCN: 研究催化剂如何工作、如何设计的化学分支
senses.example: Catalysis is now a field with its own journals and its own methods.
senses.exampleCN: 催化如今是一个有自己的期刊与方法的领域。
senses.why: any named process can become a discipline, and this noun did: the study is called by the process it studies.
senses.whyCN: 任何有名字的过程都能成为一门学科，这个名词确实如此：研究以它所研究的过程命名。

senses.title: A force that makes change easier
senses.titleCN: 使变化更易发生的中介力量
senses.definition: figuratively, any agent that lowers the resistance to a change without being used up
senses.definitionCN: 比喻用法，指降低变化阻力、自身却不被耗尽的任何因素
senses.example: The report acted as catalysis for a reform nobody had dared to start.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告成了那场无人敢启动的改革的催化。
senses.why: the metaphor keeps the whole structure of the chemical idea: a small input, no consumption, a large change.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻保留了化学概念的整体结构：输入很小、不被消耗、变化很大。

senses.title: Catalysis of social change
senses.definition: the role of an event or group that sets a wider movement going
senses.definitionCN: 某一事件或群体促使更大规模运动启动的角色
senses.example: Historians describe the strike as catalysis rather than cause.
senses.exampleCN: 历史学家把那次罢工描述为催化，而不是原因。
senses.why: commentary borrows the word to separate a trigger from a cause, just as a catalyst is not a reactant.
senses.whyCN: 评论文字借这个词把「触发」与「原因」区分开，正如催化剂不是反应物。

senses.title: Autocatalysis
senses.definition: the special case in which a product of the reaction itself acts as the catalyst
senses.definitionCN: 反应产物本身充当催化剂这一特殊情形
senses.example: Autocatalysis makes the reaction accelerate as it proceeds.
senses.exampleCN: 自催化使反应随着进行而不断加速。
senses.why: chemistry needed a short name for the loop where output feeds back as input, and built it on catalysis.
senses.whyCN: 化学需要给「产出回喂输入」的回路一个短名字，于是以 catalysis 为基础造词。

senses.title: Light-driven catalysis
senses.definition: catalysis in which light supplies the energy that drives the reaction
senses.definitionCN: 由光提供能量、推动反应的催化
senses.example: Photocatalysis on a titanium surface splits water into its gases.
senses.exampleCN: 钛表面上的光催化把水分解成两种气体。
senses.why: when the energy source rather than the catalyst is the new element, the compound name marks the difference.
senses.whyCN: 当新的要素是能量来源而不是催化剂时，复合名称便标记出这一区别。

intro.en: Catalysis is Greek: katalysis meant a dissolving or loosening, from katalyein, to dissolve, built on kata-, down, and lyein, to loosen. Berzelius gave it its chemical sense in 1835. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: catalysis 是希腊语：katalysis 意为「化解、松开」，出自 katalyein「使化解」，由 kata-「向下」与 lyein「松开」构成。贝采利乌斯在 1835 年赋予它化学义。年代均为约数。

items.en: Lyein meant to loosen, release, dissolve. Its earlier Indo-European connections are reconstructions, and the form usually cited for it is not attested in any written language.
items.cn: lyein 意为「松开、释放、化解」。它更早的印欧语联系属于重构，通常引用的形式在任何有文字的语言中都没有记录。

items.en: Kata-, down, plus lyein produced katalyein, to dissolve or break up, used of a body losing its cohesion and of an army disbanding.
items.cn: kata-「向下」加 lyein 构成 katalyein「化解、分解」，可用于物体失去结合，也可用于军队解散。

items.en: The noun katalysis named a dissolving or a release, and in later Greek also a means of ending something; it carried no chemical sense.
items.cn: 名词 katalysis 指「化解、释放」，在后来的希腊语中也指结束某事的手段；它并无化学含义。

items.en: Jöns Jacob Berzelius introduced catalysis for the strange power by which certain substances set reactions going without taking part in them.
items.cn: 贝采利乌斯引入 catalysis，指某些物质推动反应却不参与其中的那种奇特能力。

items.en: Nineteenth-century fermentation studies and twentieth-century chemical plants extended the word to enzymes and to reactors alike.
items.cn: 19 世纪的发酵研究与 20 世纪的化工厂把这个词同时扩展到酶与反应器。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Greek history of lyein is unsettled, and the reconstructed Indo-European root offered for it is a hypothesis rather than a demonstrated form.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深源头）：lyein 在希腊语之前的历史没有定论，为它提出的重构印欧词根只是假说，并非已证实的形式。

note.en: The first group is the same Greek stem in its other shapes, easily confused in writing; the second group names neighbouring ways of making a process go faster.
note.cn: 第一组是同一希腊词干的其他形态，在写作中极易混淆；第二组是意思相邻的「让过程加快」的说法。

entries.definition: The substance that performs catalysis; the -yst ending marks the agent, not the process.
entries.definitionCN: 执行催化作用的物质；词尾标出施动者，而不是过程。

entries.definition: The adjective describing anything that works by catalysis, as a converter or a cracker.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，描述任何以催化方式工作的东西，如转化器或裂化装置。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to bring catalysis about; American spelling uses -yze.
entries.definitionCN: 表示「使发生催化」的动词；美式拼写用 -yze。

entries.definition: A loop within catalysis where the product is its own catalyst; it is a special case, not a synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 催化内部的一种回路，产物自己充当催化剂；它是特例，不是同义词。

entries.definition: The act of making something ready to react; catalysis lowers the energy needed, while activation supplies it.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物进入可反应状态；催化降低所需能量，活化则提供能量。

entries.definition: A general word for speeding up; it says nothing about a catalyst or about being recovered unchanged.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指加快；不涉及催化剂，也不涉及反应后原样回收。

entries.definition: In catalysis research, promotion is the boosting of a catalyst by a small added substance, not catalysis itself.
entries.definitionCN: 在催化研究中，助催是少量添加物提升催化剂效果，并非催化本身。

entries.definition: Making an outcome easier without doing the work; close to the figurative sense of catalysis but without the chemistry.
entries.definitionCN: 使结果更容易达成而不亲自去做；接近催化的比喻义，但没有化学内容。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Greek root, the real word family and real laboratory phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的希腊词根、真实的同族词与真实的实验室说法。

normal.en: Kata- down plus lyein to loosen: the barrier is loosened, so the reaction runs.
normal.cn: kata-「向下」加 lyein「松开」：障碍被松开，反应就跑起来。

normal.en: The family runs catalysis, catalyst, catalytic, catalyse and autocatalysis.
normal.cn: 同族词有 catalysis、catalyst、catalytic、catalyse 与 autocatalysis。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the branch: heterogeneous catalysis, enzyme catalysis, industrial catalysis.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出分支：多相催化、酶催化、工业催化。

normal.en: The catalyst is never the reactant: it goes in and comes out, which is the whole point of the word.
normal.cn: 催化剂从来不是反应物：它进去又出来，这正是这个词的全部要点。

normal.en: The 1835 date belongs to Berzelius, who gave an old Greek noun its modern chemical job.
normal.cn: 1835 年这个年份属于贝采利乌斯，是他让一个古老的希腊名词承担了现代化学的职务。

abstract.en: Picture a tunnel that shortens a mountain without moving any of the rock.
abstract.cn: 想象一条隧道缩短了一座山，却没有搬走任何一块岩石。

abstract.en: Picture a match that lights a whole field and is not burned itself.
abstract.cn: 想象一根火柴点亮整片田野，自己却没有被烧掉。

abstract.en: Picture a stranger who opens a locked door and walks away before anyone enters.
abstract.cn: 想象一个陌生人打开一扇锁着的门，在任何人进去之前就走了。

examples.en: Catalysis by an acid can turn alcohol into ether at moderate heat.
examples.cn: 酸催化可以在中等温度下把醇变成醚。

examples.en: The plant doubled its output by improving catalysis rather than buying new reactors.
examples.cn: 工厂靠改进催化而非购置新反应器使产量翻倍。

examples.en: The discovery acted as catalysis for an entire branch of chemistry.
examples.cn: 这一发现成了整个化学分支的催化。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「cata（向下）+ lysis（松开）」——把阻力松下来，反应就快了 → 催化作用

root: 希腊 kata-「向下」+ lyein「松开」→ katalysis「化解、松开」→ 1835 年贝采利乌斯用作化学术语 catalysis；lyein 的更早来源无定论。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one act: a barrier is lowered and a process runs faster without the helper being used up. The act then enters cells, factories, a research field, social commentary, a feedback loop and a light-driven variant.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：障碍被降低，过程加快，而帮手并未被消耗。这个动作随后进入细胞、工厂、研究领域、社会评论、反馈回路，以及一种由光驱动的变体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tunnel opened beside a steep road, with the same walkers arriving sooner.
core.cn: 核心意象：陡路旁开出一条隧道，还是那些人，却更早到达。

branches.en: THE MECHANISM: a barrier falls and the same reaction needs less energy.
branches.cn: 机理：障碍落下，同一个反应所需能量变少。

branches.en: THE CELL: enzymes perform the same trick at body temperature.
branches.cn: 细胞：酶在体温下做同一套把戏。

branches.en: FROM PLANT TO DISCIPLINE: what works in a reactor becomes a field with its own journals.
branches.cn: 从工厂到学科：在反应器里奏效的事，变成有自己期刊的领域。

branches.en: THE METAPHOR: a small trigger that is not spent and starts a large change.
branches.cn: 比喻：一个不被消耗的小小触发，启动一场大变化。

branches.en: VARIETIES: the product that catalyses itself, and light that pays the energy bill.
branches.cn: 变体：催化自身的产物，以及替能量买单的光。

intro.en: Catalysis is built from a Greek prefix and a Greek verb, with a Greek noun ending; the modern chemical compounds add Latin and English pieces on top.
intro.cn: catalysis 由希腊前缀、希腊动词与希腊名词词尾构成；现代化学的复合词又在其上叠加拉丁语与英语成分。

latinIntro.en: This word is entirely Greek; the Latin-looking forms in the family come through scientific Latin, which simply transliterated the Greek pieces.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词完全是希腊语；词族中看似拉丁的形式都经科学拉丁语转写而来，实际只是把希腊成分音译。

items.example: The prefix gives the sense of a downward loosening.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀给出「向下松开」的意思。

items.example: The verb supplies the image of a bond coming apart.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供「结合被拆开」的意象。

items.example: Greek used it of bodies and of disbanded troops.
items.exampleCN: 希腊语用它指物体分解，也指军队解散。

items.example: The ending turns the verb into the name of a process.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把动词变成过程名称。
催化作用使催化剂本身保持不变。

items.example: The catalyst is recovered at the end of the run.
items.exampleCN: 催化剂在运行结束时被回收。

items.example: A catalytic converter cleans the exhaust.
The enzyme catalyses the breakdown of starch.
items.exampleCN: 这种酶催化淀粉的分解。

items.meaningCN: 由产物自身进行的催化
items.example: Autocatalysis can make a reaction run away.
items.exampleCN: 自催化可能让反应失控加速。

items.example: Photocatalysis needs a surface that absorbs light.
items.exampleCN: 光催化需要能吸光的表面。

definition_zh: 大灾难；毁灭性结局；悲剧的收场；彻底失败
definition_en: a sudden, widespread and ruinous event, or the disastrous end of a process
core_image: 舞台上的幕布在一个转身之间砸落，台上所有布景一次全毁
scene: 地震后的港口只剩扭曲的吊车与倾覆的货轮，经济学家称这场连锁崩塌为大灾难。The harbour after the earthquake held only twisted cranes and a capsized freighter, a catastrophe that economists traced through every linked industry.
sceneCN: 这里 catastrophe 指「范围广、破坏彻底且带有终结意味的灾难」（第 1 个义项：造成全面毁灭的重大灾变）；句意为地震后的港口只剩扭曲吊车与倾覆货轮，经济学家称这场连锁崩塌为大灾难。可辨识物件：扭曲吊车、倾覆船体、断裂栈桥、漂浮货柜。

pos.zh: 大灾难；毁灭性结局（可数）

forms.label: 相关形容词（戏剧结局的）

derivatives.zh: 把小事想成灾难；灾难化

senses.title: A ruinous event on a wide scale
senses.titleCN: 范围广泛的毁灭性事件
senses.definition: a sudden event that destroys lives, property or systems on a large scale
senses.definitionCN: 突然发生、大规模摧毁生命、财产或体系的事件
senses.example: The dam failure was a catastrophe for four downstream towns.
senses.exampleCN: 大坝失事对下游四个城镇是一场大灾难。
senses.why: the Greek original meant an overturning, so the word's core is a whole order turned over at once.
senses.whyCN: 希腊原义是「翻转」，因此这个词的核心是一整套秩序被一次掀翻。

senses.title: The final ruin of a drama
senses.definition: the closing turn of a tragedy in which the hero's fortune is destroyed
senses.definitionCN: 悲剧的收场转折，主人公的命运在此被彻底毁掉
senses.example: In the last scene the catastrophe arrives not as death but as recognition.
senses.exampleCN: 在最后一幕，灾难性的收场不是死亡，而是认出真相。
senses.why: Aristotle used the word for the final change of fortune, and English drama criticism kept that technical sense.
senses.whyCN: 亚里士多德用这个词指命运的最终转变，英语戏剧评论保留了这个专门义。

senses.title: A total failure of a plan
senses.titleCN: 计划或尝试的彻底失败
senses.definition: an attempt or arrangement that ends in complete failure
senses.definitionCN: 以彻底失败告终的尝试或安排
senses.example: The launch was a catastrophe: the rocket never left the pad.
senses.exampleCN: 这次发射是一场彻底的失败：火箭根本没离开发射台。
senses.why: the ruin is no longer physical; what is overturned is the expectation built around the plan.
senses.whyCN: 毁灭不再是物理上的，被掀翻的是围绕计划建立起来的期待。

senses.title: A sudden change in a system
senses.definition: an abrupt, discontinuous change in a mathematical or physical system
senses.definitionCN: 数学或物理系统中突然、不连续的变化
senses.example: Catastrophe theory models how a bridge's curve jumps from one shape to another.
senses.exampleCN: 突变理论研究桥面曲线如何从一个形状跳到另一个。
senses.why: mathematics borrowed the overturning image for a fold in a surface where a small push causes a large jump.
senses.whyCN: 数学借用了「翻转」意象，指曲面上某一折处：轻推一下，结果却大幅跳变。

senses.title: An ecological collapse
senses.definition: the collapse of an ecosystem past a threshold from which it cannot return
senses.definitionCN: 生态系统越过阈值、无法回到原状的崩溃
senses.example: Once the reef bleached, the fishery slid toward catastrophe.
senses.exampleCN: 珊瑚礁一旦白化，渔业便滑向崩溃。
senses.why: ecologists use the word for a threshold crossing because the old state really is overturned, not merely damaged.
senses.whyCN: 生态学家用它指越过阈值，因为旧状态是真的被掀翻了，而不只是受损。

senses.title: A humanitarian emergency
senses.definition: a crisis in which a large population loses shelter, food or medical care at once
senses.definitionCN: 大量人口同时失去住所、食物或医疗的危机
senses.example: Aid agencies warned of a humanitarian catastrophe if the border stayed closed.
senses.exampleCN: 援助机构警告，若边界持续关闭，将出现人道主义灾难。
senses.why: the word scales the harm to a population, which is why agencies pair it with humanitarian.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把损害放大到一个群体，因此机构常把它与人道主义一词搭配。

senses.title: The catastrophic ending of a story
senses.titleCN: 故事或局势的灾难性结局
senses.definition: the irreversible disastrous outcome toward which a story or situation is moving
senses.definitionCN: 故事或局势正走向的、不可逆的灾难性结局
senses.example: Every negotiation that ignored the debt was heading for the same catastrophe.
senses.exampleCN: 每一场无视债务的谈判都走向同一个灾难结局。
senses.why: the dramatic sense spread to ordinary narrative: a plot's final overturning can be economic or political.
senses.whyCN: 戏剧义扩展到日常叙事：情节的最终翻转可以是经济的，也可以是政治的。

senses.title: Abstract: any overwhelming ruin
senses.definition: a metaphorical label for any overwhelming ruin that feels final and total
senses.definitionCN: 隐喻标签，指任何显得彻底且终结性的压倒性毁灭
senses.example: The review called the film a catastrophe, and the box office agreed.
senses.exampleCN: 评论把这部电影称为一场灾难，票房也印证了这一点。
senses.why: the metaphor keeps only the core of total overturning, dropping every physical detail.
senses.whyCN: 隐喻只保留「彻底翻转」这一核心，丢掉了所有物理细节。

intro.en: Catastrophe comes from Greek katastrophē 'an overturning', built on kata- 'down' and strephein 'to turn'. It entered English through Latin and French, first as a term of drama. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: catastrophe 来自希腊 katastrophē「翻转」，由 kata-「向下」与 strephein「转」构成。它经拉丁语与法语进入英语，最初是戏剧术语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Strephein meant 'to turn, twist'; its further origin is not established, so any reconstructed root is a hypothesis.
items.cn: strephein 意为「转、扭」；其更远来源未得到证明，任何重构词根都只是假说。

items.en: Kata- 'down' plus strephein gave katastrophē, 'an overturning, a sudden end', used of a turning point in a play.
items.cn: kata-「向下」加 strephein 构成 katastrophē「翻转、突然的终结」，用于指戏剧中的转折。

items.en: Latin took the word as catastrophа, keeping the dramatic sense of a final reversal of fortune.
items.cn: 拉丁语借作 catastrophа，保留了「命运最终逆转」的戏剧义。

items.en: French catastrophe reached English in the sixteenth century as a stage term, then widened to any great disaster by the eighteenth.
items.cn: 法语 catastrophe 于 16 世纪进入英语，先作舞台术语，到 18 世纪扩展到泛指一切大灾难。

items.en: Geology used catastrophe for sudden global change in the debate over catastrophism, and mathematics later named catastrophe theory after the same image.
items.cn: 地质学在灾变论之争中用 catastrophe 指突然的全球变化，数学后来的突变理论也沿用同一意象。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Greek history of strephein is unsettled, and the exact date when the general 'disaster' sense displaced the stage sense is unknown.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：strephein 在希腊语之前的历史未定，泛指「灾难」的义项取代舞台义的确切年代亦不可考。

note.en: Group one holds ruin words that differ in reach and cause; group two holds words for the human response or the study of such events.
note.cn: 第一组是范围与成因不同的毁灭类词；第二组指人的应对反应或对此类事件的研究。

entries.definition: From Greek astron through 'ill star': a disaster may be local, and its cause may be human or natural, so it is wider in origin but often smaller in scale.
entries.definitionCN: 经「凶星」来自希腊 astron：disaster 可大可小，成因可人为可自然，因此来源更宽而规模常更小。

entries.definition: From Latin calamitas 'loss, damage': it stresses the distress people feel rather than a whole order overturned.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 calamitas「损失、损害」：强调人们承受的苦难，而非整套秩序的翻转。

entries.definition: Greek kataklysmos 'a deluge': it stresses an overwhelming physical rush, especially water or upheaval.
entries.definitionCN: 希腊 kataklysmos「洪水」：强调压倒性的物理冲击，尤其是水或地壳剧变。

entries.definition: From French débâcle, a breaking up of ice in a river: a spectacular collapse or rout, usually of a plan or an army.
entries.definitionCN: 来自法语 débâcle「河中冰层崩解」：指壮观的崩溃或溃败，多用于计划或军队。

entries.definition: A serious drama with a sorrowful end; as a general noun it stresses grief and pity, while catastrophe stresses the ruin itself.
entries.definitionCN: 以悲伤结局收场的严肃戏剧；作一般名词时强调悲痛与怜悯，而 catastrophe 强调毁灭本身。

entries.definition: From Greek krisis 'decision': the decisive moment that may end well or badly, so it precedes the catastrophe rather than naming it.
entries.definitionCN: 来自希腊 krisis「决断」：可能好也可能坏的决胜时刻，因此在灾难之前，而不是灾难本身。

entries.definition: A sudden situation calling for immediate action; it names the period of response, not the scale of the ruin.
entries.definitionCN: 指需要立即行动的突发状况；它指响应时段，而非毁灭的规模。

entries.definition: The geological view that Earth's history was shaped by sudden global upheavals; it is a doctrine about catastrophes, not one itself.
entries.definitionCN: 地质学观点，认为地球历史由突然的全球剧变塑造；它是关于灾变的学说，本身不是灾变。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real set phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: kata- means down and strephein means turn, so catastrophe is a turning down, an overturning.
normal.cn: kata- 表示「向下」，strephein 表示「转」，catastrophe 就是「向下翻转」，即倾覆。

normal.en: The stage sense came first: the catastrophe is the final reversal of a tragedy.
normal.cn: 舞台义最先出现：catastrophe 是悲剧中命运的最终逆转。

normal.en: The adjective is catastrophic, as in catastrophic flooding or a catastrophic failure.
normal.cn: 形容词是 catastrophic，如灾难性洪水或灾难性故障。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the scale: environmental catastrophe, humanitarian catastrophe.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出规模：环境大灾难、人道主义灾难。

normal.en: Geology and mathematics keep technical uses: catastrophism and catastrophe theory.
normal.cn: 地质学与数学保留专业用法：灾变论与突变理论。

abstract.en: Picture a stage curtain falling in the middle of the play and taking the set with it.
abstract.cn: 想象幕布在戏演到一半时落下，把布景一起带倒。

abstract.en: Picture a sheet of ice on a river breaking all at once with a sound like a shot.
abstract.cn: 想象河面冰层轰然一次崩裂，响声如同枪响。

abstract.en: Picture a folded map where one crease, once pressed, flips the whole sheet.
abstract.cn: 想象一张折过的地图，按下其中一道折痕，整张纸便翻面。

examples.en: The failure of the levee was a catastrophe that reshaped the city for a generation.
examples.cn: 堤坝失事是一场大灾难，重塑了这座城市整整一代人。

examples.en: Ignoring the early warnings turned a manageable flood into a catastrophe.
examples.cn: 无视早期预警，把一场可控的洪水变成了大灾难。

examples.en: In the final act the catastrophe is a recognition, not a death.
examples.cn: 在最后一幕，悲剧的收场是一次认出，而非一死。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「cat（猫）+ astro（星）+ phe」——猫盯着灾星，一次翻身全毁 → 大灾难

root: 希腊 katastrophē「翻转」= kata-「向下」+ strephein「转」，经拉丁 catastrophа 与法语进入英语；strephein 的更深来源不确定。英语 catastrophe。

sensesIntro.en: Eight meanings follow one overturning: first a whole order destroyed, then the stage reversal, then any plan or system that flips, and finally the metaphor for total ruin.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一次「翻转」展开：先是整套秩序被毁，再是舞台上的逆转，接着是计划或系统的翻转，最后是对彻底毁灭的隐喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a whole set is overturned in a single movement.
core.cn: 核心意象：整套布景在一次动作中被掀翻。

branches.en: SCALE OF HARM: the overturning is measured by how many lives and systems go down with it.
branches.cn: 损害规模：翻转的轻重，取决于多少生命与体系随之倒下。

branches.en: DRAMATIC ARC: the stage reversal and the story's ending share one final turn.
branches.cn: 戏剧弧线：舞台逆转与故事结局共用同一次最终转折。

branches.en: PLAN FAILURE: nothing physical breaks, but the expectation is overturned.
branches.cn: 计划失败：没有实物破碎，被掀翻的是期待。

branches.en: SYSTEM THRESHOLD: mathematics and ecology both describe a small push that flips a state.
branches.cn: 系统阈值：数学与生态学都描述「轻推一下、状态翻面」。

branches.en: METAPHOR: only the claim of total finality survives when the word is used loosely.
branches.cn: 隐喻：宽泛使用这个词时，只剩「彻底且终结」这一主张。

intro.en: Catastrophe is a Greek compound whose two parts also build a small family of English technical words, so it can be read morpheme by morpheme.
intro.cn: catastrophe 是一个希腊复合词，两部分还构成一小族英语技术词，因此可以按语素逐个读出。

latinIntro.en: The Greek prefix kata- appears in cataclysm and catalog; the root strephein appears in strophe and in the technical adjective catastrophic.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊前缀 kata- 出现在 cataclysm 与 catalog 中；词根 strephein 出现在 strophe 与形容词 catastrophic 中。

items.example: The prefix turns the movement downward.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把动作转向下方。
那场洪水是一场大灾难。

items.meaning: a turning away to address someone
items.example: The poem opens with an apostrophe to the night.
items.exampleCN: 这首诗以对夜的呼告开篇。

items.meaning: the doctrine of sudden global change
items.exampleCN: 灾变论曾与均变论相抗衡。

items.meaning: to treat a small trouble as ruin
items.example: She tends to catastrophize a single mistake.
items.exampleCN: 她容易把一次错误想成灾难。

latinEntries.structure: catastrophа, catastrophae (f., first declension, Latinized Greek)
latinEntries.meaning: an overturning; the final turn of a play
a turn, a stanza sung while turning

definition_zh: 灾难性的；毁灭性的；造成彻底失败的
definition_en: causing or involving ruin on a very large scale
core_image: 一排多米诺骨牌从第一张开始连锁倒下，最后一张砸穿了地板
scene: 洪水退去后，粮仓只剩空架，农会估计损失足以让全镇破产，形容为灾难性后果。When the floodwater withdrew, only the empty frame of the granary remained, and the farm board called the losses catastrophic enough to bankrupt the whole town.
sceneCN: 这里 catastrophic 指「造成大范围、近乎不可挽回的破坏」（第 1 个义项：后果具毁灭性）；句意为洪水退去后粮仓只剩空架，农会称损失之大足以让全镇破产。可辨识物件：空粮仓骨架、倒伏的骨牌、泡水的账册、破堤口。

pos.zh: 灾难性的；毁灭性的（多作定语，也可作表语）

senses.title: Causing ruin on a large scale
senses.definition: causing destruction that is widespread and hard to reverse
senses.definitionCN: 造成广泛且难以逆转的破坏
senses.example: The storm surge had a catastrophic effect on the low-lying districts.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴潮对低洼城区造成了灾难性影响。
senses.why: the adjective simply carries the noun's overturning into a modifier: whatever it touches is turned over.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词只是把名词的「翻转」带进修饰位置：它触到的东西都被掀翻。

senses.title: Disastrous as an outcome
senses.definition: ending in complete and damaging failure
senses.definitionCN: 以彻底且有害的失败告终
senses.example: The decision to ignore the engineers proved catastrophic.
senses.exampleCN: 无视工程师意见的决定被证明是灾难性的。
senses.why: nothing physical is destroyed here; what collapses is the plan and the trust behind it.
senses.whyCN: 这里没有实物被毁，崩塌的是计划以及支撑计划的信任。

senses.title: Involving enormous financial loss
senses.definition: producing losses so large that they threaten the survival of the organisation
senses.definitionCN: 造成的损失之大，危及组织本身的存续
senses.example: Insurers class a single storm as catastrophic once claims pass a fixed threshold.
senses.exampleCN: 一旦赔款超过固定门槛，保险公司就把单场风暴列为灾难性事件。
senses.why: the insurance industry turned the adjective into a threshold label for losses that break a balance sheet.
senses.whyCN: 保险业把这个形容词变成门槛标签，专指足以击穿资产负债表的损失。

senses.title: Of a drama's final reversal
senses.definition: belonging to the closing reversal in which a tragedy's fortunes are destroyed
senses.definitionCN: 属于悲剧命运被彻底毁掉的收场转折
senses.example: The playwright keeps the catastrophic scene off stage and reports it in a messenger's speech.
senses.exampleCN: 剧作家把这一灾难性的场面留在幕后，由传信人的台词转述。
senses.why: drama criticism kept the technical sense, using the adjective for the moment when the reversal lands.
senses.whyCN: 戏剧评论保留了这一专门义，用该形容词指逆转落地的那一刻。

senses.title: Of a sudden geological upheaval
senses.definition: describing a sudden worldwide change in the earth's crust or climate
senses.definitionCN: 描述地壳或气候的突然全球性变化
senses.example: Catastrophic eruptions can cool the whole planet for a year.
senses.exampleCN: 灾难性的火山喷发能让整个行星降温一年。
senses.why: geology needed a word for change by sudden event rather than slow accumulation, and borrowed this one.
senses.whyCN: 地质学需要一个词指「由突发事件造成的变化」而非缓慢累积，于是借用了它。

senses.title: Severe and irreversible in medicine
senses.titleCN: 医学上严重且不可逆的
senses.definition: describing an illness or injury that is severe, sudden and permanently damaging
senses.definitionCN: 描述严重、突发且造成永久损害的疾病或损伤
senses.example: The policy covers catastrophic illness but not routine care.
senses.exampleCN: 这份保单覆盖重大疾病，但不含日常诊疗。
senses.why: medicine borrowed the financial threshold label: the illness is catastrophic because of its cost and permanence, not its cause.
senses.whyCN: 医学借用了财务门槛标签：疾病之所以「灾难性」，在于费用与不可逆，而非成因。

senses.title: Of an abrupt jump in a system
senses.definition: describing a discontinuous change in which a small shift produces a large jump
senses.definitionCN: 描述一种不连续变化：微小移动带来巨大跳变
senses.example: The model predicts a catastrophic jump once the load passes the fold point.
senses.exampleCN: 模型预测，一旦荷载越过折点，就会出现灾难性跳变。
senses.why: catastrophe theory used the word for the fold in a surface, so the adjective marks the jump itself.
senses.whyCN: 突变理论用这个词指曲面上的折处，因此形容词标记的是跳变本身。

senses.title: Abstract: overwhelmingly harmful
senses.definition: used loosely for anything felt to be overwhelmingly harmful or badly judged
senses.definitionCN: 宽泛地用于任何被认为极其有害或判断极糟的事物
senses.example: Calling the merger catastrophic was an exaggeration, but the lost jobs were real.
senses.exampleCN: 把这次合并称为灾难性有些夸张，但失去的工作岗位是真的。
senses.why: the loose use keeps only the intensity of the original: something is judged as if it had been overturned.
senses.whyCN: 宽泛用法只保留原词的强度：某事物被判定得仿佛被掀翻过一样。

intro.en: Catastrophic is the adjective of catastrophe, the Greek katastrophē 'overturning', plus the Greek adjectival ending -ikos. It reached English through Latin and French. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: catastrophic 是大灾难 catastrophe 的形容词，由希腊 katastrophē「翻转」加希腊形容词词尾 -ikos 构成，经拉丁语与法语进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Katastrophē 'an overturning' came from kata- 'down' plus strephein 'to turn'; the deeper origin of strephein is not established.
items.cn: katastrophē「翻转」由 kata-「向下」加 strephein「转」构成；strephein 的更远来源未得到证明。

items.en: -ikos was the ordinary Greek ending for 'belonging to, of the nature of', so katastrophikos meant 'of an overturning'.
items.cn: -ikos 是希腊语中表示「属于、具有……性质」的常用词尾，因此 katastrophikos 意为「翻转性质的」。

items.en: Latin -icus and French -ique carried the ending into English -ic, which by the seventeenth century attached freely to nouns of Greek origin.
items.cn: 拉丁 -icus 与法语 -ique 把这个词尾带入英语 -ic，到 17 世纪它已能自由附着于希腊来源的名词。

items.en: Catastrophic appears in English drama criticism before it spreads to ordinary description of floods, wars and failures.
items.cn: catastrophic 先出现在英语戏剧评论中，之后才扩展到对洪水、战争与失败的日常描述。

items.en: Insurance fixed catastrophic loss as a threshold term, and medicine followed with catastrophic illness; geology used it in the catastrophism debate.
items.cn: 保险业把 catastrophic loss 定为门槛术语，医学随后有 catastrophic illness；地质学在灾变论之争中也使用了它。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Greek history of strephein is unsettled, and no exact first citation is recorded for the insurance sense, so the dates given are approximations.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：strephein 在希腊语之前的历史未定，保险义也没有确切的最早书证，所给年代均为约数。

note.en: Group one holds adjectives that differ in what they blame or how final the harm is; group two holds the nouns and adverbs that share the same root.
note.cn: 第一组是归因或终结程度不同的形容词；第二组是同根的名词与副词。

entries.definition: Built on Greek klyzein 'to wash', so it stresses a flood-like physical rush rather than a whole order overturned.
entries.definitionCN: 由希腊 klyzein「冲洗」构成，强调洪水般的物理冲击，而非整套秩序被翻转。

entries.definition: From Greek apokalypsis 'unveiling': it borrows the imagery of a final world-ending revelation, a much larger claim.
entries.definitionCN: 来自希腊 apokalypsis「揭开」：借用世界终结式启示的意象，语气比 catastrophic 大得多。

entries.definition: A rare adjective built directly on catastrophe with -al; it exists but is far less common than catastrophic.
entries.definitionCN: 直接由 catastrophe 加 -al 构成的罕用形容词，存在但远不如 catastrophic 常用。

entries.definition: From Latin fatum 'fate': it means causing death or doom, and says nothing about the size of the loss.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 fatum「命运」：指致死或注定失败，不涉及损失规模。

entries.definition: The plainer adjective from disaster; it can describe a merely bad dinner, which catastrophic rarely does.
entries.definitionCN: 由 disaster 来的更日常的形容词，可以形容一顿很糟的晚餐，而 catastrophic 很少这样用。

entries.definition: From Latin devastare 'to lay waste': it stresses the sweeping destruction of an area or a person's feelings.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 devastare「荒废」：强调对地区或人的情感造成的横扫式破坏。

entries.definition: From Latin ruina 'a falling down': it points at collapse, especially of finances, and is more formal and literary.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 ruina「倒塌」：指向崩塌，尤指财务，语气更正式、更书面。

entries.definition: From Latin calamitas 'loss': it emphasises the distress borne by people rather than the mechanism of the disaster.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 calamitas「损失」：强调人们承受的苦难，而非灾害的机制。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real set phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The base is catastrophe, a turning down; -ic makes it an adjective of that overturning.
normal.cn: 词基是 catastrophe「向下翻转」，-ic 使其成为表示该翻转的形容词。

normal.en: The -ic ending is the same one in dramatic, poetic and historic.
normal.cn: 这里的 -ic 与 dramatic、poetic、historic 中的 -ic 相同。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the professional uses: catastrophic failure, catastrophic illness, catastrophic loss.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出专业用法：灾难性故障、重大疾病、灾难性损失。

normal.en: The adverb is catastrophically, as in catastrophically wrong.
normal.cn: 副词是 catastrophically，如错得灾难性地。

normal.en: Geology pairs it with catastrophism, the doctrine of sudden upheaval.
normal.cn: 地质学把它与灾变论配对，后者主张突然剧变。

abstract.en: Picture a row of dominoes where the first tile is no bigger than a coin.
abstract.cn: 想象一排多米诺骨牌，第一张不过硬币大小。

abstract.en: Picture a bank statement where one line wipes out every column.
abstract.cn: 想象一张银行对账单，其中一行抹掉了所有栏目。

abstract.en: Picture a small crack that lets a whole reservoir through a wall.
abstract.cn: 想象一道小裂缝，让整座水库穿墙而过。

examples.en: A single missed inspection can be catastrophic for a dam.
examples.cn: 一次漏检对一座大坝可能是灾难性的。

examples.en: The company called the recall catastrophic but kept its factories open.
examples.cn: 公司称这次召回是灾难性的，却仍让工厂开工。

examples.en: Catastrophic eruptions are rare, which is why their traces are so clear.
examples.cn: 灾难性的火山喷发很罕见，正因此留下的痕迹格外清晰。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「cat（猫）+ astro（星）+ phic」——灾星压顶，连锁全毁 → 灾难性的

root: 希腊 katastrophē「翻转」（kata- 向下 + strephein 转）加希腊形容词词尾 -ikos，经拉丁 -icus 与法语 -ique 进入英语 -ic；strephein 更深来源不确定。英语 catastrophic。

sensesIntro.en: Eight meanings follow one adjective: ruin by physical force, ruin by failed planning, ruin by cost, then the stage reversal, the sudden earth change, the medical threshold, the mathematical jump and finally ordinary exaggeration.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个形容词展开：物理力量的毁灭、谋划失败造成的毁灭、代价造成的毁灭，再到舞台逆转、地球突变、医学门槛、数学跳变，最后是日常的夸张用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one touch sends a whole row down and breaks the floor.
core.cn: 核心意象：轻轻一触，整排倒下，地板被砸穿。

branches.en: SCALE AND COST: physical ruin and financial ruin are both measured by how much cannot be recovered.
branches.cn: 规模与代价：物理毁灭与财务毁灭，都以「有多少无法挽回」来衡量。

branches.en: JUDGEMENT: when nothing physical breaks, the word becomes a verdict on a decision.
branches.cn: 评判：没有实物破碎时，这个词就成了对某项决定的判词。

branches.en: FINAL JUMPS: the drama's last reversal and the model's fold are both irreversible jumps.
branches.cn: 终结性跳变：戏剧的最后逆转与模型的折点，都是不可逆的跳变。

branches.en: EARTH SCALE: geology applies the adjective to change that arrives as an event, not a trend.
branches.cn: 地球尺度：地质学把这个形容词用于「以事件形式到来」而非趋势性的变化。

branches.en: MEDICAL THRESHOLD: an illness becomes catastrophic when cost and permanence cross a line.
branches.cn: 医学门槛：当费用与不可逆性越线，疾病便成为「灾难性」的。

intro.en: The word is transparent: a Greek-derived noun plus the Greek-Latin adjective ending -ic, and both parts recur across English.
intro.cn: 这个词很透明：一个源自希腊语的名词加希腊—拉丁形容词词尾 -ic，两部分在英语中都反复出现。

latinIntro.en: Greek strophe and the prefix kata- build catastrophe and cataclysm; Latin -icus gives the English ending -ic, as in historic and dramatic.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 strophe 与前缀 kata- 构成 catastrophe 与 cataclysm；拉丁 -icus 给出英语词尾 -ic，如 historic 与 dramatic。

items.exampleCN: 那场洪水是一场大灾难。

items.exampleCN: 灾变论把化石解释为洪水沉积。

items.example: The catastrophist argued for a sudden flood.
items.exampleCN: 这位灾变论者主张发生过一场突发洪水。

items.meaning: to treat a small trouble as ruin
items.example: Do not catastrophize one bad result.
items.exampleCN: 不要把一次糟糕的结果灾难化。

items.example: The cataclysm left a layer of silt.
items.exampleCN: 那场剧变留下一层淤泥。
